articles.t: GTA 6 Trailer Remade in GTA 5 Shows Incredible Differences
articles.chapeau: A fan-made GTA 6 trailer recreation in GTA 5 showcases just how dramatically the series has changed visually in the over 10 years between releases.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 Trailer Remade in GTA 5 Shows Incredible Differences From GameRant (Written by Drew Swanson) on October 20, 2026 | OpenCritic
With GTA 6 officially one month away from launch, it's almost unbelievable that its predecessor looks the way it did. One GTA 6 fan has recreated the game's trailer in GTA 5 to show just how big a graphical jump there is between the two entries. The differences are night and day, showing just how impressive the tech behind GTA 6 and its rendition of Vice City is in 2026.
It's safe to say that GTA 6 is one of the most anticipated games of the past decade , especially since it's been over 13 years since GTA 5 was originally released. In that time, the landscape of the gaming industry has changed dramatically, as has the technology that powers its development and the hardware that runs it. As such, it's no surprise that GTA 6 looks leagues better than its predecessor, but the dramatic difference between the two entries far outpaces the rest of the franchise.
GTA 6 will qualify for consideration at The Game Awards 2026 even with an exceedingly late November 19 launch.

articles.t: Gestion des armes dans GTA 6 : Rockstar ne voulait pas d’une roue des armes traditionnelle mais a dû s’en contenter
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 sort dans exactement un mois, et Rockstar a présenté le jeu à travers de longues séquences de gameplay ainsi que deux bandes-annonces. La récente bande-annonce de lancement est venue compléter le tout, mais de nombreux détails ont été révélés au fil d’interviews, de fuites et d’autres sources.
articles.txt:
Il y a longtemps, lorsque des fuites concernant GTA 6 ont commencé à faire surface, et on parle d’ il y a environ un an , la roue des armes est devenue un sujet de discussion. À l’époque, on pensait que Rockstar voulait une roue des armes dans le style de Red Dead Redemption 2 pour GTA 6 , avec notamment une roue des armes pour le coffre de la voiture. Nous savons maintenant que c’est la direction qu’a prise Rockstar, mais il s’avère que le studio a dû se rabattre sur cette solution.
Le journaliste Jason Schreier a récemment publié un long article sur le développement de GTA 6 . Bien qu’il contienne beaucoup d’informations, certains détails n’ont pas été retenus dans la version finale. L’un d’eux concernait la roue des armes de GTA 6 . Nous avons maintenant vu à quoi elle ressemble, et elle est devenue un sujet de discorde parmi les fans en raison de son apparence « bizarre ».
Schreier a mentionné dans sa vidéo que, même si l’intention avait toujours été de proposer un système plus réaliste, comme dans Red Dead Redemption 2 (RDR 2), les développeurs voulaient à l’origine une interface complètement différente. Les développeurs de Rockstar ont « passé des mois, voire des années » à concevoir un autre système de sélection des armes, avec notamment des plateaux, des toiles et d’autres options, mais ils n’ont rien trouvé qui fonctionne aussi bien. Ils ont donc décidé de se rabattre sur la roue des armes.
Ce réalisme à la RDR 2 signifie que les joueurs ne pourront pas transporter un arsenal massif sur eux. Il a été révélé qu’ils pourront porter un pistolet, deux armes à longue portée et une arme de corps à corps. Ils pourront également utiliser le coffre des voitures pour stocker davantage d’armes.

articles.t: GTA 6 Is Wiping Out PS5 Pro Stock a Month Before Launch - CNET
articles.chapeau: The game's exclusivity is leading to greater demand for the high-end console.
articles.txt:
Rockstar’s extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6 aired in late August. Within a few weeks, the PlayStation 5 Pro was gone from every major US retailer. Buyers who want the best possible version of the year’s biggest game are gravitating to Sony’s top console, especially with no PC version planned for launch. A global memory chip shortage that’s raised hardware prices all year has made the squeeze worse, and Sony has warned retailers it’ll last into 2027.
Part of the reason for high console demand is that GTA 6 will be exclusive to PlayStation 5/Pro and Xbox Series X/S when it comes out on Nov. 19, and no other platforms have been announced yet.
In September, Sony reportedly advised distributors that the PlayStation 5 Pro would be in short supply until 2027, citing “temporary market supply constraints and high demand.” The most severe bottleneck limiting PlayStation distribution is a global crisis in memory and storage components driven by the AI infrastructure squeeze, or RAMageddon .
The PS 5 Pro promises better frame rates for a number of games as well as enhanced 4K processing, while the Rockstar Studios game is also designed to work on the “vanilla” PS5.
Yet, GTA 6 isn’t the only recent high-profile PlayStation release: The PS5-exclusive Wolverine — by the makers of Spider-Man and Spider-Man 2 — has reportedly sold 2.16 million copies since September.
The PlayStation 5 Pro debuted in November 2024 for $700, but its retail price has since increased to $900.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the long-awaited sequel to Grand Theft Auto 5 , which first appeared in 2013. The crime-based game reportedly offers a playable area twice the size of the previous game’s. It’s available for preorder for $80.
Representatives for Sony didn’t respond immediately to CNET’s request for more information.

articles.t: Pourquoi GTA est un jeu en monde ouvert ? On ne s'attendait pas à cette réponse
articles.chapeau: Cela fait bientôt trente ans que la franchise GTA existe et alors que GTA 6 débarque dans moins d'un mois, les développeurs originaux nous révèlent le secret du monde ouvert, élément devenu indissociable du titre.
articles.txt:
Cela fait bientôt trente ans que la franchise GTA existe et alors que GTA 6 débarque dans moins d’un mois, les développeurs originaux nous révèlent le secret du monde ouvert, élément devenu indissociable du titre.
On vous parle d’un temps où Rockstar Games n’était pas un studio surpuissant capable de vous vendre une boîte sans disque tout en vous regardant droit dans le globe oculaire, sachant très bien qu’on va tous se jeter sur leur GTA 6 le 19 novembre prochain. Parce que oui, impossible d’éviter le mastodonte vidéoludique, même si vous ne comptez pas y jouer. Un titre que l’on attend particulièrement pour sa liberté, issue d’ un monde ouvert qui a forgé sa réputation depuis l’arrivée du tout premier Grand Theft Auto en 1997. Pourtant, ce même monde ouvert était loin d’être une évidence pour les développeurs de l’époque, à un détail près.
Il y a quasiment trente ans, Rockstar s’appelait encore DMA Design (de 1988 à 2002) et plusieurs membres du studio au moment de GTA premier du nom ont récemment participé à une table ronde sur les origines du titre, lors du Games Day 2026 de la Scottish Game Developers Association à Dundee, en Écosse. Parmi eux, le directeur créatif de DMA, Gary Penn , partage ses souvenirs d’un projet Grand Theft Auto qui n’avait rien à voir avec le jeu finalement sorti : “ce concept de monde ouvert ne faisait pas partie du jeu. L’expérience était très linéaire et on choisissait les missions dans le menu.”
Mais alors d’où vient l’idée de changer la formule pour celle qui fera des millions de dollars de recettes ? D’un éclair de génie ou du beau bordel qui régnait dans les bureaux à ce moment-là ? “Il est certain qu’à cette époque, c’était très désordonné” , confie Penn. Le programmeur principal Keith Hamilton enfonce le clou en s’amusant : “Honnêtement, l’idée du monde ouvert est née du fait que nous ne voulions pas avoir à créer d’interface . On commence un niveau, et c’est tout, on continue.” En gros, le monde ouvert était plus “simple” à créer que de s’embêter à faire un suivi d’histoire linéaire avec l’interface de jeu qui allait avec. Le monde ouvert dans GTA ? Le résultat d’une bonne grosse flemme .
Du coup, le jeu a remplacé l’interface par des missions données par des cabines téléphoniques auxquelles on pouvait répondre dans un ordre aléatoire. “Les missions s’intègrent naturellement à cet espace et soudain, le jeu change du tout au tout, l’expérience devient complètement différente.” Une inspiration qui vient de Die Hard 3 : Une journée en enfer , même si plus personne ne semble savoir pourquoi (on vous rappelle que c’était il y a trente ans et que l’organisation n’était pas leur leitmotiv).

articles.t: GTA 6 : Rockstar confirme des centaines de lieux accessibles, et vous pourrez même préparer vos braquages
articles.chapeau: À l’approche du 19 novembre 2026, Rockstar promet un Vice City métamorphosé, où des centaines d’intérieurs accessibles bousculent la routine des braquages. Entre Jason, Lucia et une police plus tenace que jamais, GTA 6 cache encore quelques surprises sur la façon de s’y préparer.
articles.txt:
À l’approche du 19 novembre 2026, Rockstar promet un Vice City métamorphosé, où des centaines d’intérieurs accessibles bousculent la routine des braquages. Entre Jason, Lucia et une police plus tenace que jamais, GTA 6 cache encore quelques surprises sur la façon de s’y préparer.
Rockstar Games promet de bouleverser la visite de Vice City avec Grand Theft Auto VI, attendu le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Lors d’une présentation à Rockstar North, le studio a confirmé que la carte de l’état de Leonida regroupera des centaines d’intérieurs interactifs, accessibles en exploration libre pour vivre, se cacher… et préparer vos braquages avec Jason et Lucia.
Dans la démo décrite par le site spécialisé Allkeyshop et par le journaliste Jason Schreier du média économique américain Bloomberg, les deux héros passent sans chargement d’un parc à une salle de sport, puis à une banque ou à l’arrière-boutique d’une station-service. Chaque porte ouverte ajoute des options de gameplay : repérage, cambriolage discret, dépôt d’argent volé, bien loin des rares intérieurs de Grand Theft Auto V .
Lors de cette preview organisée à Édimbourg, les directeurs Aaron Garbut, Phil Hooker et Rob Nelson ont détaillé un monde ouvert pensé pour l’intérieur autant que pour la rue. Allkeyshop explique que ces lieux vont des salles de sport aux banques en passant par les boutiques, et qu’ils disposent tous de mécaniques dédiées. Des sites français comme PlanetGTA6 rappellent toutefois que Rockstar parle seulement de « des centaines » d’intérieurs, sans chiffre précis ni garantie que chaque bâtiment soit ouvert en permanence.
Dans la séquence montrée à la presse, Rob Nelson fait appeler Lucia par Jason pour une sortie banale. Ils traversent un parc main dans la main, passent par une salle de sport où chacun s’entraîne, puis entrent dans une banque pour jauger la sécurité. Le casse paraît trop risqué : le duo vise alors l’arrière-boutique d’une station-service, désactive l’alarme, ramasse les billets et s’éclipse sans que la police ne réagisse.
Le site communautaire GTAVIFRANCE rapporte qu’à ce moment de la démo, un membre de Rockstar lâche qu’il y a « tellement de petits intérieurs, des centaines ». L’expression « gta 6 centaines d’intérieurs accessibles » ne relève donc pas du fantasme : chaque supérette ou station-service peut devenir un repaire ou une cible. Allkeyshop souligne que l’argent circule physiquement sur le personnage et qu’il faut le déposer dans une banque ou un DAB pour le mettre à l’abri des flics comme des rivaux.
Allkeyshop décrit aussi un système de recherche repensé : la police identifie Jason et Lucia comme un duo et suit le couple comme une seule cible lors des poursuites. Se séparer oblige alors les patrouilles à se diviser, tandis que les intérieurs offrent des itinéraires de fuite, des planques temporaires ou des points de rupture de ligne de vue. Ce système de traque devient un terrain de jeu idéal pour exploiter la densité de GTA 6 .
Rockstar rapproche d’ailleurs l’histoire de Jason et Lucia de celle de Red Dead Redemption 2 plutôt que du trio explosif de Grand Theft Auto V . Plutôt que des disputes permanentes, le duo partage des activités du quotidien – promenade au parc, séance de sport, virée à la banque – qui se transforment en préparation de casse dès que l’envie de braquer un lieu accessible se fait sentir.

articles.t: GTA 6 Map Update Reveals New Buildings, Enterable Locations, and Size Comparisons
articles.chapeau: The latest GTA 6 mapping project update reveals more detailed buildings, roads, and potential enterable locations across Leonida, including Star Island, Vice Beach, Milport, and Gables Estates. Comparisons with previous Rockstar games suggest that GTA 6 could feature a significantly larger world than GTA 5, offering diverse environments and more opportunities for exploration.
articles.txt:
The latest GTA 6 mapping project update reveals more detailed buildings, roads, and potential enterable locations across Leonida, including Star Island, Vice Beach, Milport, and Gables Estates. Comparisons with previous Rockstar games suggest that GTA 6 could feature a significantly larger world than GTA 5, offering diverse environments and more opportunities for exploration. As players prepare for the game's expansive world and future progression opportunities, those interested in the in-game economy may also want to buy GTA 6 Money to support their adventures.
The GTA 6 mapping project began in 2022, when early leaks provided the community with its first clues about the game's world. Since then, contributors have continuously refined the map using official promotional materials, gameplay footage, and other available information.
The interactive map allows users to explore individual locations and view the screenshots or trailers used to identify them. Recent additions include more detailed building layouts, expanded road networks, and markers highlighting locations that players may be able to enter.
However, not every building has been fully identified. Locations marked in blue represent buildings that the community has identified as enterable, while unmarked structures may still prove accessible in the finished game.
Several notable areas have received substantial improvements in the latest update.
Star Island has gained additional buildings, offering a clearer picture of its luxury residential areas. Based on the available map information, the island could feature some of Vice City's most expensive mansions.
Vice Beach has also received more detailed building layouts and several confirmed potential interior locations. Official promotional images frequently showcase this area, suggesting that its beachfront streets, nightlife, and surrounding businesses will play an important role in the game.
Catalan Key has become more developed, with additional structures and numerous potential enterable buildings. These locations could include shopping centers, hotels, nightclubs, and jewelry stores, although their exact functions remain unconfirmed.
Port Gellhorn has also received more detail. Some newly mapped locations appear to resemble trailer parks and coastal residential areas, reflecting the variety of environments expected across Leonida.
The industrial area known as Goliath, reportedly inspired by the real-world Titan America steelworks, now features additional buildings and roadways. These changes provide a better understanding of the industrial infrastructure surrounding the region.
The mapped prison has also expanded slightly as contributors incorporated additional aerial views. The revised boundaries suggest a larger facility than previously estimated, although the final in-game layout has yet to be verified.
The Thrillbilly Mud Club, featured in Rockstar's promotional footage, now has a more detailed layout. New map information reveals additional structures and surrounding terrain, helping players understand the location before release.
Milport has also received new details, including large cranes extending over the water. These structures suggest a significant cargo port designed to accommodate maritime transportation and industrial activity.
Waning Sands now includes a large outdoor shopping complex that the mapping community believes resembles a mall in Orlando, Florida. Its blue marker indicates that the location is considered enterable, with its open-air design potentially allowing players to explore shops and walkways without entering a single enclosed building.
Gables Estates has gained additional residential structures and a tennis court. The area's large properties suggest another wealthy neighborhood, alongside Star Island and the exclusive golf community associated with the Lynx Golf Club.
The growing number of identified interiors is one of the most interesting aspects of the latest map update. Gas stations, stores, police stations, nightclubs, and other commercial locations have been identified using available footage.
These discoveries suggest that GTA 6 could offer a more detailed urban environment, with opportunities to explore businesses and residential properties throughout Leonida. Nevertheless, the community's current markings should not be treated as a complete list of accessible interiors.
The latest comparison places the projected GTA 6 map alongside the maps from previous Rockstar titles.

articles.t: GTA 6 Is So Massive, Even Rockstar's Developers Don't Know Every Detail
articles.chapeau: Rockstar's latest GTA 6 revelations are fascinating. Hundreds of interiors, unexpected details added by developers, and a weapon system that almost looked completely different.
articles.txt:
Facebook X Pinterest ason and Lucia in Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated open-world adventure set in Vice City and the state of Leonida. Image credit: Rockstar Games. Rockstar Games has packed so much into Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) that even its own developers don’t know everything the game contains. According to Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut, no single person has a complete picture of the project.
The revelation comes from Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier, who recently visited Rockstar’s Edinburgh studio for an extensive behind-the-scenes report. Beyond the game’s enormous scale, Rockstar has revealed hundreds of explorable interiors, surprising details about its development process, and why the familiar weapon wheel almost didn’t make the cut.
“There’s no one person that has this whole thing in their head” , Garbut told Schreier, highlighting the sheer complexity of developing GTA 6.
In a follow-up video accompanying his Bloomberg investigation, Schreier explained that Rockstar gives individual developers considerable creative freedom. Artists and designers can introduce small environmental details simply because they believe those additions would improve the game.
One amusing example comes from Red Dead Redemption 2. The game’s horses famously have anatomically accurate testicles that shrink in cold weather. According to Garbut, that wasn’t a feature ordered by management or included in some massive development checklist. A developer simply decided it would be a cool detail to implement.
Schreier believes GTA 6 will contain plenty of similar surprises, potentially including things even senior developers haven’t personally encountered.
Rockstar’s workforce has also grown substantially. The company now employs 4,711 people across 12 offices, nearly doubling its 2,441 employees when Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in 2018.
See also : GTA 6’s New Trailer Gets Steamy as Jason and Lucia Share an Intimate Moment
Rockstar’s attention to detail extends well beyond the streets of Vice City. During Schreier’s visit, development head Rob Nelson demonstrated how protagonists Jason and Lucia interact with the world. The pair could spend time together, visit a gym, scout potential robbery targets, and carry out crimes without following a conventional mission sequence.
One demonstration involved sneaking into a gas station’s back office, disabling its alarm, and stealing cash without attracting attention. Rockstar also revealed that GTA 6 contains hundreds of smaller interiors that players can enter and explore.
That’s particularly exciting for longtime GTA fans. Exploring a massive city is one thing, but having more buildings to enter and interact with could make Vice City and the surrounding state of Leonida feel considerably more alive.
Rockstar hasn’t provided an exact number of accessible interiors, although the reported scale already represents one of the game’s more promising improvements.

Another interesting revelation concerns GTA’s familiar weapon-selection system. According to Schreier, Rockstar spent months, potentially years, experimenting with alternatives to the traditional weapon wheel. Developers tried different interfaces, including tray-like and web-style layouts, before ultimately returning to the familiar circular design.
The challenge came from Rockstar’s desire to make GTA 6 more grounded, borrowing elements from Red Dead Redemption 2. Unlike GTA 5, where players can carry an enormous arsenal, Rockstar wanted a more restrictive weapon system that would require players to think about their loadouts.
However, replacing the weapon wheel proved more difficult than expected. Rockstar eventually retained the familiar interface rather than forcing a less intuitive alternative.
It’s an interesting example of how even seemingly simple gameplay mechanics can require extensive experimentation during development.

articles.t: GTA 6's Story Is Closer To Red Dead Redemption 2 Than GTA 5
articles.chapeau: Bloomberg's Jason Schreier says GTA 6's story feels closer in tone to Red Dead Redemption 2 than the "sour nihilism" of GTA 5.
articles.txt:
Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier says Grand Theft Auto VI’s story feels more inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2 than Grand Theft Auto V, calling that shift welcome in his newsletter on the game’s development . Schreier wrote that GTA 5’s “sour nihilism” got tiring fast, saying he recently replayed the 2013 game’s opening hour and felt exhausted by characters who spend most of their time insulting and yelling at each other.
He contrasted that with Jason and Lucia, describing their story as one about two people who genuinely enjoy spending time together.
Schreier’s read on the story lines up with comments Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson gave to TroisCouleurs earlier this year, where he said the team wanted to bring the same emotional depth and connection players felt with Red Dead Redemption 2’s Arthur Morgan into GTA 6.
Rockstar has built Jason and Lucia’s relationship as the center of the story rather than a side element, a structural shift from GTA 5’s three separate, loosely connected protagonists in Michael, Franklin, and Trevor.
Schreier also touched on GTA 6’s new systemic gameplay, saying he’s curious whether features like its evolved NPC interactions and relationship systems stay engaging over a long playthrough or end up feeling more like a novelty. GTA 6 launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
For more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, check out eXputer’s GTA 6 news roundup and the recent Game Informer feature on Leonida’s world, weather, and wildlife.

articles.t: GTA 6 Cyberleek update: Leaker linked GTA 6 reveals to crypto play. It’s crashing spectacularly.
articles.chapeau: The Cyberleek memecoin is now plunging further and further.
articles.txt:
As Mashable and our colleagues at PCMag just reported, Grand Theft Auto VI leakers Cyberleek have seemingly abandoned their threats to leak a full build of the game – at least for now.
Why? Because the leakers had claimed that the release of the leaked build was tied to their memecoin. If GTA 6 fans pumped Cyberleek's cryptocurrency, they would receive the leaked game build as a reward.
That play failed spectacularly for Cyberleek. In fact, it seems to have fully backfired.
The Cyberleek memecoin's market cap hit a high of $7.8 million on October 11, shortly after the leakers claimed they would release the full build of GTA 6 supposedly in their possession. The catch? The Cyberleek memecoin had to hit a market cap of $30 million first.
While some GTA 6 fans appeared to have bought into the memecoin in an attempt to hit Cyberleek's goal, $7.8 million is still far short of the $30 million the leakers wanted. And since then, as it became obvious that most GTA 6 fans weren't going to give in to Cyberleek's demands, the memecoin has plunged even further, with a current market cap of $1.17 million.
Critics of Cyberleek celebrated the memecoin's failure, calling it a scam.
Cyberleek had been successful with their memecoin play before, giving those who bought their memecoin exclusive access to polls that determined what GTA 6 footage the leakers would release next.
However, it seems Cyberleek overplayed their hand this time around, and the full build, which they claim is 200GB, appears to be staying under wraps for now.
With that said, Cyberleek is still using their supposed access to a full build of GTA 6 to try to escape legal action from Take-Two, the parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games. The leakers claim that there is a "dead-man's switch" that will automatically release the ending of the game if there is an attempt to take down Cyberleek.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' file size: Cyberleek reveals eye-watering storage requirements
articles.chapeau: Take it with a grain of salt, of course.
articles.txt:
The person leaking a bunch of gameplay videos of Grand Theft Auto VI may have just revealed the most useful information in all of their leaks.
On the Cyberleek website (per our colleagues at PCMag ), one of the latest updates included a threat to release a full build of the game in some form if people on the internet raised the leaker's crypto memecoin to a $30 million market cap. The coin has since crashed and looks like it's not going to get anywhere close to that level, but more importantly, the update included a file size for the playable build they have evidently been taking clips from: 200GB.
That's obviously a huge number, and makes up more than 20 percent of the usable storage space on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X console. Perhaps surprisingly, it's not as big as some other games, as recent Call of Duty titles clear 200GB by a good margin. But it would still be one of the biggest single-player file sizes we've seen yet, and speaks to the scale and scope of GTA 6 .
Of course, this should be taken with at least a tiny bit of skepticism. We don't know much about the build Cyberleek has been leaking footage from. If they do indeed have the full game on hand, it could be an older build that hasn't been fully optimized yet, so the true GTA 6 file size could theoretically be smaller once the actual game comes out on Nov. 19.

articles.t: PS5 console jailbreak on latest 14.10 firmware shared before GTA 6 release date
articles.chapeau: PlayStation may have hoped it would take longer to compromise the current 14.10 firmware. However, a homebrew developer has found a way to exploit Sony's software. The PS5 console jailbreak could enable piracy of games like GTA 6 that require the update.
articles.txt:
Recently, there has been progress in finding a PS5 jailbreak for the latest 14.10 firmware . Homebrew developer Gezine has now shared a video showing access to the console’s debug settings . While dumping games still faces obstacles, the news reintroduces a piracy threat as the GTA 6 release date approaches.
After Sony blocked exploits in the October 1st software update, Gezine claims to have overcome the security protections. That said, several reasons explain why supporters aren’t yet celebrating. The commonly used hypervisor bypass , which is key to creating and booting game backups, isn't working.
Another issue is that the PS5 console jailbreak is private, and it’s unclear if the developer will upload the files. Doing so could attract Sony’s attention and prompt new firmware to counter the advancement. Some followers are already asking for a delay until the November 19th GTA 6 release date arrives.
The PlayStation homebrew scene has evolved rapidly in the last several months. It hit a milestone in late July when the Relapse exploit became compatible with the 13.60 software rollout. Previously, gamers had to search for much older hardware that hadn’t been updated. 14.00 and 14.10 thwarted hackers, but it appears the measures were only temporary.
More attention has focused on the PS5 jailbreak because of Rockstar’s next title. A datamine of the PlayStation backend reportedly discovered that GTA 6 would require firmware 14.10 to run. That raised a dilemma for homebrew enthusiasts, since the latest software impeded Relapse and the Byepervisor Reborn bypass.
Although they may no longer have to compromise, a working backup of the crime epic is not guaranteed. Apps like the Overdrive store make it easier to find and boot games. Still, not all titles perform smoothly, and the Rockstar project is particularly demanding .
With piracy on the rise, both Sony and publishers may be monitoring Gezine’s efforts. Even if the hacker refuses to release the exploit, multiple developers are probing PS5 consoles for weaknesses.

articles.t: GTA 6 : Prochaines annonces, nouveau gameplay et surprises avant le lancement
articles.chapeau: À l’approche de la sortie de GTA 6, Rockstar intensifie sa campagne marketing avec des publicités spectaculaires, des véhicules inspirés du jeu et des installations dans plusieurs grandes villes. Mais alors que le trailer de lancement est déjà disponible, plusieurs semaines restent avant la sortie. Rockstar pourrait-il préparer d’autres révélations, notamment un aperçu du gameplay, des informations sur la version PC ou des détails sur GTA 6 Online ? Voici les principales pistes à surveiller.
articles.txt:
À l’approche de la sortie de GTA 6, Rockstar intensifie sa campagne marketing avec des publicités spectaculaires, des véhicules inspirés du jeu et des installations dans plusieurs grandes villes. Mais alors que le trailer de lancement est déjà disponible, plusieurs semaines restent avant la sortie. Rockstar pourrait-il préparer d’autres révélations, notamment un aperçu du gameplay, des informations sur la version PC ou des détails sur GTA 6 Online ? Voici les principales pistes à surveiller. Pour beaucoup, ces détails incluent aussi la question de Argent GTA 6 et de la progression dans le multijoueur.
Le trailer de lancement de GTA 6 a déjà accumulé des dizaines de millions de vues en quelques jours. Ce succès n’est pas surprenant compte tenu de l’attente autour du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games. Cependant, le moment choisi pour sa publication soulève une question : pourquoi dévoiler ce trailer alors qu’il reste encore environ un mois avant la sortie ?
Habituellement, les trailers de lancement apparaissent quelques jours avant la commercialisation d’un jeu. Ils sont souvent courts, durant environ une minute à une minute et demie, afin de pouvoir être adaptés à différentes campagnes publicitaires, notamment à la télévision.
Red Dead Redemption 2 fournit un exemple intéressant. Son trailer de lancement est sorti le 18 octobre 2018, seulement huit jours avant la sortie du jeu, le 26 octobre.
GTA 6 suit donc un calendrier marketing différent. La publication anticipée de son trailer pourrait permettre à Rockstar de maintenir l’attention du public pendant plusieurs semaines, avant de dévoiler d’autres informations. Cela ne garantit toutefois pas qu’un nouveau trailer arrivera prochainement.
L’un des signes les plus visibles de cette campagne est l’arrivée de publicités GTA 6 dans le monde réel. Miami, qui sert d’inspiration à Vice City, semble occuper une place centrale dans cette stratégie.
À Times Square, à New York, un immense panneau publicitaire consacré au jeu attire l’attention. Des bus décorés aux couleurs de GTA 6 ont également été signalés à Chicago, tandis que Miami accueille plusieurs installations particulièrement spectaculaires.
Un dirigeable aux couleurs du jeu survole la ville, et un bâtiment affiche le message « Welcome to Vice City ». Des décorations supplémentaires sont apparues sur des structures urbaines, notamment sous un pont dont les couleurs rappellent l’identité visuelle de GTA 6.
La campagne ne se limite pas aux panneaux d’affichage. Des parasols et des installations de plage reprennent également le thème du jeu à Miami Beach. À Wynwood, des artistes réalisent des fresques inspirées de l’univers de Vice City, avec des personnages et des éléments visuels qui évoquent les images déjà dévoilées.
D’autres publicités ont été repérées à West Hollywood et sur un bâtiment en France. Cette présence internationale montre que Rockstar cherche à toucher un public bien plus large que les joueurs qui suivent quotidiennement l’actualité du jeu.
Parmi les opérations promotionnelles les plus originales figurent plusieurs voitures réelles inspirées des véhicules de GTA 6.
Des supercars reprenant l’apparence de leurs équivalents virtuels ont été aperçues dans les rues de Miami. Elles portent notamment des plaques d’immatriculation associées à l’État fictif de Leonida, renforçant le lien entre la campagne publicitaire et l’univers du jeu.
Le convoi comprendrait une Lamborghini transformée en voiture de police de Vice City, ainsi qu’une McLaren inspirée de la Progen Emerus. Ces véhicules permettent de transposer directement dans le monde réel le style automobile caractéristique de GTA 6.
Des vidéos montrent également ces voitures circulant dans la ville, accompagnées de musique associée à la campagne promotionnelle. Sur les plages, les panneaux, les parasols et les autres installations créent une ambiance qui rappelle certaines images du jeu.
L’ensemble donne l’impression que Rockstar transforme temporairement plusieurs quartiers de Miami en une version réelle de Vice City. Cette stratégie renforce la visibilité du jeu avant son lancement, même si elle ne révèle pas directement de nouvelles fonctionnalités.
Depuis la fin août, Rockstar semble avoir organisé plusieurs annonces autour d’un rythme hebdomadaire. Les révélations se sont succédé : aperçu étendu, manettes PlayStation aux couleurs de GTA 6, précommandes, album, édition collector, reportage consacré au jeu, produits dérivés, stations de radio et enfin trailer

articles.t: GTA 6 conçu sans IA générative : sur PC, ce sont les moddeurs qui décideront
articles.chapeau: Take-Two martèle que l’IA générative n’a joué aucun rôle dans GTA 6. Cette promesse s’arrête aux portes du studio : la version PC, attendue quelques mois après
articles.txt:
Ajoutez-nous sur Google Depuis près d’un an, Take-Two martèle une promesse au sujet de Grand Theft Auto VI : aucune IA générative n’a été utilisée pour le créer. Strauss Zelnick a expliqué aux investisseurs et aux journalistes que les villes de Rockstar étaient façonnées à la main, et qu’un modèle entraîné sur les données d’hier n’aurait pas pu les concevoir. Un argument convaincant pour un lancement auquel Take-Two a lié l’ensemble de son exercice financier. C’est aussi une promesse qui concerne le studio, mais ne dit rien des personnes qui posséderont le jeu.
Cette distinction cesse d’être théorique le jour où GTA VI arrive sur PC. Les joueurs sur console découvrent le monde livré par Rockstar. Ceux sur PC, eux, peuvent ouvrir les fichiers. La date de cette deuxième sortie, que Rockstar n’a toujours pas confirmée, est la décision de lancement la plus lourde de conséquences qui reste à prendre chez Take-Two, davantage encore que la date sur console que l’entreprise a déjà dû repousser.
Les propos de Zelnick étaient précis. S’exprimant auprès de GamesIndustry.biz avant la publication des résultats du troisième trimestre de Take-Two, il a déclaré que l’IA générative « n’a absolument aucun rôle dans ce que construit Rockstar Games », comme l’a rapporté ESPN, et décrit des univers conçus « bâtiment par bâtiment, rue par rue, quartier par quartier ». Lors d’un événement organisé par CNBC l’automne précédent, il avait soutenu que la propriété intellectuelle créée avec l’IA « n’est pas protégeable » et que les résultats seraient « assez dérivatifs », selon PCGamesN. Dans le même temps, Take-Two mène, d’après ESPN, des centaines de projets pilotes liés à l’IA dans d’autres secteurs de l’entreprise afin de gagner du temps et de réduire les coûts. La limite porte sur la création, pas sur les activités de l’entreprise.
Ce message répondait aussi aux attentes du marché. Les déclarations sur l’« absence totale de rôle » de l’IA ont suivi l’annonce de Project Genie par Google , qui promettait des univers jouables générés par l’IA et coïncidait avec une baisse des valeurs du secteur du jeu vidéo, dont celle de Take-Two. En un mot, le fait main relève à la fois du positionnement produit et du message rassurant adressé aux investisseurs.
Les versions console sont des boîtes fermées. La version PC, elle, peut être démontée par les joueurs, qui restent libres de choisir les outils qu’ils veulent utiliser, y compris l’IA. La promesse de Take-Two ne peut pas accompagner le jeu jusque-là.
La précédente sortie avait laissé à Rockstar une longue marge de manœuvre. Grand Theft Auto V est arrivé sur consoles en septembre 2013, puis sur PC en avril 2015, soit environ un an et demi plus tard. Un article publié ce mois-ci par GamesBeat, qui cite quatre sources anonymes du secteur et a été repris par VICE, situe la sortie de la version PC de GTA VI au premier trimestre 2027. Rockstar n’a pas répondu à GamesBeat, et une fenêtre de sortie évoquée dans la presse ne constitue pas une date de lancement. Si cette échéance se confirme, la période durant laquelle Rockstar décide seule de ce que contient son univers se réduira à quelques mois, au lieu de plusieurs années.
Rockstar a déjà traversé ce genre de situation, et son parcours est instructif. En 2015, l’entreprise a banni l’équipe à l’origine de FiveM, le mod qui permettait aux joueurs de GTA V de gérer leurs propres serveurs multijoueurs de jeu de rôle, en le qualifiant de « service multijoueur alternatif non autorisé contenant du code conçu pour faciliter le piratage », comme l’a relaté Game World Observer. Huit ans plus tard, cette même équipe, Cfx.re, est devenue « officiellement une partie de Rockstar Games », selon des modalités non divulguées. Rockstar a déclaré avoir élargi sa politique en matière de mods afin d’inclure officiellement les créations de la communauté de jeu de rôle, rapporte 80 Level.
Cette trajectoire résume la logique commerciale. Rockstar a d’abord combattu la scène, puis l’a intégrée une fois que les serveurs de jeu de rôle étaient devenus un moteur de la popularité de ses jeux sur Twitch. Il s’est avéré plus intéressant de posséder la plateforme que de la réprimer. La question reste entière pour GTA VI : Rockstar adoptera-t-elle cette approche dès le premier jour de la sortie PC ou, comme avec FiveM, attendra-t-elle des années, le temps que les joueurs bâtissent ce qu’elle voudra ensuite récupérer ?

articles.t: GTA 6 Was Built Without Generative AI. The PC Version Lets Players Bring It In
articles.chapeau: Take-Two insists generative AI had no part in building GTA 6. That promise stops at the studio door, and a PC version reportedly months behind console is where
articles.txt:
Add us on Google Take-Two has spent the better part of a year making one promise about Grand Theft Auto VI with unusual force: no generative AI went into it. Strauss Zelnick has told investors and interviewers that Rockstar’s cities are built by hand, and that a model trained on yesterday’s data could not have made them. It is a sound pitch for a launch Take-Two has tied its whole financial year to. It is also a promise about the studio, and says nothing about the people who will own the game.
That distinction stops being academic the day GTA VI reaches PC. Console players get the world Rockstar shipped. PC players get files they can open. The timing of that second release, which Rockstar has still not confirmed, is the most consequential launch decision left on Take-Two’s desk, more so than a console date the company has already had to move.
Zelnick’s wording has been precise. Speaking to GamesIndustry.biz ahead of Take-Two’s third-quarter results, he said generative AI “has zero part in what Rockstar Games is building”, as ESPN reported, describing worlds made “building by building, street by street, neighborhood by neighborhood”. At a CNBC event the previous autumn he argued that intellectual property created with AI is “not protectable” and that the output would be “pretty derivative”, according to PCGamesN. Meanwhile Take-Two runs what ESPN describes as hundreds of AI pilots elsewhere in the company to save time and money. The line is drawn around creation, not around the business.
The message also answered the market. The “zero part” remarks followed Google ’s Project Genie announcement, which promised AI-generated playable worlds and coincided with a fall in games stocks, Take-Two’s among them. Handcrafted is product positioning and investor reassurance in a single word.
Console versions are locked boxes. The PC version is the one players can take apart, and whatever tools they bring with them, AI included, are theirs to choose. Take-Two’s pledge cannot follow the game there.
Precedent gave Rockstar a long runway last time. Grand Theft Auto V reached consoles in September 2013 and PC only in April 2015, a gap of about a year and a half. A GamesBeat report this month, citing four unnamed industry sources and relayed by VICE, puts GTA VI’s PC version in the first quarter of 2027. Rockstar did not respond to GamesBeat, and a reported window is not a release date. If it holds, the period in which Rockstar alone decides what its world contains shrinks from years to months.
Rockstar has been here before, and the record is instructive. In 2015 it banned the team behind FiveM, the mod that let GTA V players run their own multiplayer roleplay servers, calling it an “unauthorized alternate multiplayer service that contains code designed to facilitate piracy”, as Game World Observer recounted. Eight years later the same team, Cfx.re, became “officially a part of Rockstar Games”, on undisclosed terms. Rockstar said it had expanded its mod policy to officially include work by the roleplay community, according to 80 Level.
That arc is the business logic in miniature. Rockstar fought the scene first, then brought it inside once roleplay servers had become a driver of its games’ popularity on Twitch. Owning the platform turned out to be worth more than suppressing it. The open question for GTA VI is whether Rockstar takes that position on day one of the PC release or, as with FiveM, years after players have built the thing it later wants.
Take-Two’s August results reiterated a forecast of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in net bookings for the fiscal year ending next March, and Zelnick tied that guidance directly to the November 19 launch. The filing lists GTA VI for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and names the company’s dependence on its NBA 2K and Grand Theft Auto products as a risk. PC and other platforms made up 9% of net bookings in the latest quarter. The revenue is on console. The risk to the handcrafted story is on PC.
Zelnick’s argument that AI-made work is derivative and unprotectable is a defence of Take-Two’s catalogue. It offers no shield against players running the same tools on top of that catalogue. Once the PC build is out, the question of what generative AI does to GTA VI moves from Rockstar’s studios to its community, where the company’s leverage has always been its mod policy and, when that failed, bringing the modders in-house.

articles.t: Cyberleek drops new NSFW Lucia videos, threatens to release GTA 6 in full
articles.chapeau: Only about a month until the game is out.
articles.txt:
Notorious Grand Theft Auto VI leaker Cyberleek is back with a vengeance, it seems.
The anonymous video poster went dark after the big Netflix trailer in late August, but returned last week with a big, chunky 24-minute clip that featured story cutscenes, auto races, and the male protagonist Jason fully nude. Over the weekend and into Monday morning, Cyberleek shared some more clips that we won't link to, but can be easily found on social media. The new clips largely revolve around the female protagonist Lucia, and also show her completely nude, doing things like walking around Vice City or parachuting off a tall building.
In addition, Cyberleek posted a warning on their website claiming that if their memecoin reached a market cap of $30 million, they would release a video showing a full playthrough of the game's story prior to release. The same post also included a demand for publisher Take-Two to apologize for not releasing the game on disc and to rectify that issue. It is extremely unlikely the company could fire up disc manufacturing for GTA 6 in a timely fashion, even if the publisher wanted to negotiate with the leaker. At this point, there is no sign of that happening.
Just like in the videos featuring a nude Jason, the nude Lucia videos seem a little fishy in the sense that NPCs don't react to their nudity at all. Given that recent Rockstar games are built entirely around believable NPC interactions, that would suggest the nudity is not a regularly accessible feature in the final game and is being achieved through the use of developer tools.

articles.t: Zelda Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Release Date vs GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Zelda Ocarina of Time hits Switch 2 Nov. 5, just 14 days before GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox. Here is why the overlap may not matter.
articles.txt:
Nintendo and Rockstar Games are about to run one of the strangest release-calendar experiments in modern gaming. On November 5, 2026, Nintendo puts out The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. Fourteen days later, on November 19, 2026, Rockstar ships Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Gaming outlets including The Game Business, Nintendo Everything, Nintendo Life, Nintendo Wire, and Notebookcheck have spent the past several weeks asking the same question: why would Nintendo plant its biggest nostalgia bet of the decade directly in the blast radius of the most anticipated game of the generation?
The short answer, according to the bulk of current reporting, is that it might not be a blast radius at all. The two games sit on different hardware, chase different household budgets at different moments, and arrive with different kinds of risk attached. Here is what is actually confirmed about the two launches, what is still speculation dressed up as analysis, and why the zelda ocarina of time switch 2 release date landing so close to GTA VI has become the most-discussed scheduling decision of the holiday season.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Grand Theft Auto VI has carried a firm, Rockstar-confirmed release date of November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S for months, a timeline Digital Trends has tracked since the game’s earliest reveals . It is, by almost every measure, the single biggest release window in gaming this year. Publishers have spent 2026 quietly shuffling their own calendars away from that date, clearing a runway for Rockstar the way retailers clear space around a holiday blockbuster film.
Nintendo did the opposite. During a Direct presentation tied to the 40th anniversary of the Zelda franchise, the company revealed that its remake of the 1998 classic would launch November 5, 2026, a date widely reported by outlets including NME . That places the Ocarina of Time remake just 14 days ahead of GTA VI, inside the same holiday shopping window and squarely inside the same news cycle that Rockstar’s launch will otherwise dominate.
That gap is small enough to matter and large enough to be deliberate. Two weeks is roughly the amount of time a committed player needs to finish a remake of a game built for a 10-to-15-hour original campaign, padded out with new content, before a second 80-hour-plus open world absorbs their attention span entirely. It is also roughly the window retailers need to run a full cycle of launch-week promotion before a bigger story pushes it off the front page.
Strip away the speculation and the confirmed facts about GTA VI are narrow but solid. According to IGN’s tracking page for the game , Rockstar has set November 19, 2026, as the release date, and the game is confirmed only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. No PC version has been announced. No Nintendo Switch 2 version has been announced either, despite months of fan speculation and at least one round of reporting in which Nintendo addressed the possibility of a Switch 2 port without committing to one.
That platform gap is the single most important fact in this entire story. A Switch 2 owner who does not also own a PlayStation 5 or an Xbox Series X|S has no way to play GTA VI on launch day, full stop. There is no cross-shopping decision to make between the two games for that customer, because only one of them is available to them at all.
Rockstar has not issued public commentary explaining why November 19 was chosen over an earlier or later date, and no statement from the studio addresses the Zelda remake’s proximity. Readers should treat any claim about Rockstar’s internal reasoning as outlet speculation rather than confirmed company position, because that is exactly what it is right now.
Nintendo’s remake of Ocarina of Time is reported as a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive launching November 5, 2026. That date has been echoed across multiple gaming outlets since the anniversary Direct, and it is the figure this entire comparison hinges on. What is not nailed down, at least not in a form traceable to an on-record Nintendo statement, is the company’s internal reasoning for picking a date two weeks ahead of the biggest release of the console generation.

articles.txt:
UPDATE: Oct. 13, 2026, 12:34 p.m. EDT As of Tuesday afternoon, copies of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' for Xbox Series X/S are back in stock at Amazon.
If you haven't already secured a pre-order for Grand Theft Auto VI , then Amazon may not be the best place to do it.
As noted on Reddit, "physical" copies of GTA 6 were sold out on Amazon as of Monday morning, with both the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions listed as "currently unavailable."
As of this writing, the PS5 version is back in stock. Mashable reached out to Amazon to ask about GTA 6 inventory and restocks ahead of the Nov. 19 release, and we'll update this story if we receive more information.
You'll notice that I put "physical" in quotes because the game, rather infamously, will not ship on a disc.
You might be wondering how it's possible for a game that's only available as a digital download to sell out ahead of time. If you read between the lines on the Amazon store page, you can put it together. Pre-ordering via Amazon or another physical retailer will get you a box for the game, but the box will only include a download code instead of a disc, according to the fine print on Amazon.
In other words, it seems like Amazon has run out of Xbox boxes with download codes in them for the time being. articles.t: Where to buy the PS5 Pro ahead of GTA 6 release
articles.chapeau: Scalpers are asking up to $1,700 for Sony's sold-out console ahead of the 'GTA 6' launch.
articles.txt:
You'll be hard-pressed to find a PlayStation 5 Pro in stock right now. Major retailers, including PlayStation Direct , Best Buy , Amazon (including bundle offers), Target , and Walmart , are sold out. With the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI , the reseller market has gotten a little ridiculous (as has everything else).
Beyond the obvious hype for Rockstar's next release, Sony is dealing with broader supply chain bottlenecks. The global AI boom is squeezing the semiconductor market , which means Sony can't build consoles fast enough. According to distributor reports , these supply constraints could keep stock tight well into 2027.
Naturally, scalpers are having a field day. We've seen third-party listings on reseller sites (and even GameStop's official pre-owned page ) gouging buyers for $1,300 to $1,500+ for a console that retails for $899 . Sony is taking the issue so seriously that in Japan, they're forcing buyers to enter a lottery — and prove they've clocked at least 60 hours of PS4 or PS5 playtime over the last two years — just for a chance to buy a PS5 Pro.
If you absolutely have to buy one today and have money to burn, here's what the third-party market currently looks like:
Swappa: This is a legitimate, verified marketplace for used tech. However, verified PS5 Pro listings are currently sitting at $1,338.
StockX: The popular resale bidding site currently has the console hovering around $1,290.
Macy's and Walmart: Don't be fooled by third-party sellers on major retail sites. A low-rated seller on Walmart is currently asking $1,644.99 (open-box units are already sold out), while a third-party seller on Macy's is asking a staggering $1,749.99.
Mercari: We found a listing here for $800. Since this is $100 below the official MSRP for a highly coveted, sold-out item, it's almost certainly a scam. Avoid it.
If you're set on securing a Pro before launch day, here's how to play the restock game without burning a hole in your wallet:
Sign up for stock alerts. Restocks happen in small, sudden waves. Set up notifications through stock-tracking accounts on X (like @PS5StockUpdater ) or apps like HotStock to get pinged the second inventory hits.
Bookmark and refresh product pages. Keep direct product pages saved for PlayStation Direct , Best Buy , Amazon , Target , and Walmart . PlayStation Direct in particular occasionally drops invite-only or queue-based stock.
Check local inventory. Sometimes brick-and-mortar stores (like local GameStops or Target stores) receive small physical allocations that don't always show up online right away. It never hurts to ask an associate in person.
Preorder the game now. Don't hold your breath for a last-minute GTA 6 PS5 Pro console bundle. Secure your physical or digital preorder now so you're ready to go, no matter which console sits under your TV on day one.
The official retail price for a PS5 Pro is $899. If you see it listed for $1,300, $1,500, or more, you're looking at a third-party markup. Don't feed the scalpers.
Grand Theft Auto VI is currently scheduled to release November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
No, you definitely don't. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will run at 30fps on both the base PS5 and the Pro. Plus, Sony is bringing some of its newer AI upscaling technology to the base PS5 anyway, so you'll get a great visual experience on the standard hardware without spending $900.

articles.t: GTA 6 November 'rival' drops 9/10 free sample on Steam for a limited-time
articles.chapeau: It's not sticking around for too long 🦖🔥
articles.txt:
Enjoy a free Steam demo for one of the few games willing to go head-to-head with GTA 6.
The fiercest rival of GTA VI has just dropped a 9/10 rated free demo on Steam. Unfortunately, no, it’s not The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, but it is something a lot more godly.
After years of agonising waiting, GTA VI finally arrives next month, bringing all-new mayhem to Rockstar Games' modern-day Vice City.
However, this November, we’re not only being treated to GTA VI and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, but also the remaster of all remasters. We’re, of course, talking about Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered , and right now, you can play its free demo on Steam.
This playable demo is only available on PC via Steam, despite the game coming to PlayStation, Xbox Series X/S and Nintendo Switch 2. What’s more, it's also is only available on Steam until 27 October 2026.
Never fear, though, because the full game is out very soon, on 3 November 2026, across all available platforms, so at least we won’t have to wait very long to enjoy the full breadth of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered .
Originally released for Nintendo GameCube in October 2002 before arriving on Xbox the following year, Pipeworks Studio’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee quickly became a cult classic and is still viewed favourably all these years later. Hence why it’s getting a remaster after 24 years.
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee is a fighting game that lets you control iconic kaiju, including Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah, as they battle across destructible cities, causing all sorts of chaos as they go.
This release features enhanced visuals powered by Unreal Engine 5, with improved lighting, weather and destruction effects. Each kaiju has an additional campaign, and the game also features online multiplayer and much more.
It's one of very few games actually willing to brave November and launch ahead of GTA VI , which has generated plenty of memes and jokes online, plus earned the general respect of the industry.
"The ultimate Godzilla arena brawler is back, completely remastered. Choose your monster and battle it out with a range of brutal attacks through recreated cities and other locations. Face off against your friends and foes in local co-op or new online multiplayer," reads the synopsis of the game.

articles.txt:
Mark it on your calendars: November 19, 2026, is the day the world called in sick. Seems odd to think a video game could potentially cause a dip in the globe’s GDP, but the sixth iteration of the Grand Theft Auto series is easily one of the most hotly anticipated gaming releases in recent memory. Now, we’re just one month away.
Grand Theft Auto VI has been in development for over a decade and has frustrated would-be players with a couple of significant delays. The previous game debuted in 2013, so a sixth entrant in the series has been taking its sweet time coming. In a slightly shorter window of time, the Fast and Furious franchise has managed 10 feature movies and a spin-off. Of course, building out a game of epic scale is a more difficult task than just pointing a video camera at Vin Diesel and telling him to growl “family,” a dozen times.
The Grand Theft Auto launch trailer dropped late last week, and there’s plenty of wheeled content packed into it to enjoy. Famously, the game doesn't use real-life vehicle nameplates, but the in-game cars are closely modeled on actual cars you'll see in traffic. Just, in this case, flying over helicopters and whatnot.
The latest trailer kicks off with a spiderweb-painted green lowrider of some description, probably an Impala clone, then cuts to an iguana scuttling away from an R33 Nissan Skyline. Next, a character leaps from a Ford Ranger onto the landing gear of an aircraft—driving around airports in a questionable manner has long been a GTA mainstay.
We then get a close-up of the game’s two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, leaning up on a modified Chevy Camaro. The game is set in Florida, in the fictional Vice City, and you’ll be able to play out plenty of Bonnie-and-Clyde action with this pair of virtual ne’er-do-wells.
This is followed by a lime-green Bugatti Veyron (or similar) being chased by a couple of Vice City’s finest. Looks like the police cars in the game will be based on the Ford Explorer and Taurus Interceptors... expect to be seeing a lot of them.
Dirt bike jump, helicopter crash, biplane at the beach; Grand Theft Auto always crams in plenty of inventive missions for players to complete, and it looks like you’ll also need to participate in some underground street racing. A clip shows a pack of supercars speeding through the night, one of them a yellow Lamborghini Diablo.
It all looks like tremendous fun, especially as in Grand Theft Auto , there are no real-world criminal consequences for causing a police chase that’s the size of the one at the end of The Blues Brothers . Try that in your Nissan Altima; they’re gonna throw the book at you.
So, get ready, gamers, the countdown is on until Grand Theft Auto VI is ruining your productivity. Everybody else, mark down November 19th as a good day to go for a long drive. There’ll be plenty of people sitting on their couches, glued to their PlayStation, rather than on the roads.”

articles.t: GTA 6 Features "Significantly Narrower" Roads Than GTA 5; Devs Wanted Weapons System to Be More Like Red Dead Redemption 2
articles.chapeau: Rockstar confirms GTA 6 features "significantly narrower" roads than GTA 5, as they experimented on the game's weapon system for years.
articles.txt:
Vehicle chases are often a big part of any Grand Theft Auto game, and if you find it easy to drive around pedestrians and other vehicles in GTA 5, that will prove to be harder in GTA 6.
If you’re expecting Grand Theft Auto 6 to be bigger in every way compared to GTA 5, there’s at least one thing that’s now known, and that’s smaller: the roads.
This new tidbit of info might be something people noticed in the trailers, but it’s now confirmed.
In a video talking about his experience visiting Rockstar’s main studio in Scotland, Jason Schreier talked about some of the info he wasn’t able to put in his “Making Of” GTA 6 feature .
According to Art Director Aaron Garbut. the roads are “significantly narrower” in GTA 6 than they were in GTA 5.
This was something Schreier didn’t notice until the developers pointed it out. In GTA 5, which was set in a fictional representation of Los Angeles, players saw these really wide roads that made it easy to zip through the streets and bypass traffic, and speed past other cars. Players really didn’t feel any traffic of any kind, which is an unrealistic depiction of LA. This made the game feel more racing game-ish, as players were freely driving around the city.
That won’t be the case with GTA 6. Rockstar’s idea for this highly anticipated sequel is narrower roads and denser traffic, which are things the studio has decided on from the very beginning of development.
This design decision had ripple effects to the rest of development. as Garbut said, “All these things sort of come to bite you later,” since this meant denser roads, narrower roads that equated to a lot more buildings, more construction around that concept — which is what Rockstar did.
Another thing mentioned in the video is how realistic GTA 6 would be, and how much of these big systems from Red Dead Redemption 2 are going to carry over to this GTA game.
Rob Nelson, also one of the development leads, mentioned that Rockstar knew they wanted GTA 6’s weapon system to be more like Red Dead 2, where players couldn’t just carry an unlimited number of guns. Rockstar wanted it to be more realistic, where players had to select a loadout; players had to have a limited number of weapons they can hold at any given time.
Rockstar didn’t want it where players could just pull a rocket launcher out, then their guns and other stuff too. The developers’ idea was to use a weapon wheel but their concern was, wouldn’t all these blank spaces remind people of what they can’t actually do? What they can’t carry, and so on.
Rockstar second-guessed whether they should use a weapon wheel, and spent months — if not years — trying different things that would replace the weapon wheel. The devs tried trays, webs, and all sorts of different variations in the UI to just replace the weapon wheel. They even tried not having one, and after trying all these different iterations, they wound back where they started: with a weapon wheel, which is what players will see in the final version of GTA 6.
I’m interested in how these narrower roads will work in the game. It will probably make chases much more exciting and action-packed, and not to mention, way harder.
In related GTA 6 news, the developers revealed that players can expect “hundreds” of interior spaces that can be explored .

articles.chapeau: Red Dead Redemption 3 pourrait sortir en 2028 selon Citi. Découvrez les dernières rumeurs sur sa sortie, son histoire et ses futurs personnages.
articles.txt:
Red Dead Redemption 3 pourrait bien arriver plus tôt que prévu, avec une sortie potentielle en 2027 ou 2028. C'est du moins l'hypothèse avancée par la banque d'investissement américaine Citi , qui s'est penchée sur les finances de Take-Two Interactive et le coût de développement de GTA 6 . Une analyse qui remet sur la table le retour de la célèbre franchise western de Rockstar Games , huit ans après la sortie de Red Dead Redemption 2 . Mais entre projections financières et véritables informations sur le jeu, il y a encore quelques kilomètres de désert à traverser à cheval...
L'information remonte au 15 octobre 2026 . Dans une note destinée aux investisseurs, Citi estime qu' un nouveau Red Dead pourrait débarquer en 2027 ou 2028 , une perspective jugée « pas déraisonnable » par les analystes de la banque américaine.
L'analyse repose sur un élément financier intéressant: le budget colossal de GTA 6 ne serait finalement pas aussi astronomique que certaines estimations le laissaient entendre...
Dans une interview accordée à Bloomberg le 14 octobre, Jennifer Kolbe , responsable de l'édition chez Rockstar Games, a effectivement démenti les estimations plaçant le développement de GTA 6 au-delà de 1,5 milliard de dollars , sans pour autant communiquer son véritable budget.
Or, Citi relève que Take-Two comptabilise environ 2,4 milliards de dollars de coûts de développement de logiciels activés . Une différence théorique d'environ 900 millions de dollars qui pourrait, selon la banque, suggérer l'existence d'un autre projet particulièrement ambitieux dans les cartons de l'éditeur. Et difficile de ne pas penser à Red Dead Redemption.
Red Dead Redemption - Rockstar Games & Take-Two Attention toutefois: ces 900 millions ne représentent pas un budget officiellement réservé à Red Dead Redemption 3 . Les chiffres concernent les activités de Take-Two dans leur ensemble, et non exclusivement Rockstar. Citi formule donc une hypothèse financière, pas une révélation sur un jeu tenu secret.
Reste que cette perspective a de quoi rassurer les investisseurs: un nouveau Red Dead permettrait à Take-Two d'enchaîner deux énormes sorties après GTA 6 , actuellement attendu le 19 novembre 2026, et d'éviter une trop forte baisse de revenus après le lancement de son mastodonte.
Il faut effectivement rappeler un détail qui a son importance: Rockstar Games n'a toujours pas annoncé officiellement Red Dead Redemption 3 . Aucun teaser , aucune fenêtre de sortie, aucune plateforme et encore moins de présentation du gameplay.
Le calendrier imaginé par Citi apparaît d'ailleurs très optimiste . Red Dead Redemption est sorti en 2010, GTA 5 en 2013, Red Dead Redemption 2 en 2018, et GTA 6 doit arriver en 2026. Les productions majeures de Rockstar sont désormais espacées de plusieurs années, avec des développements toujours plus complexes.
Lucia Caminos et Jason Duval, les protagonistes de GTA VI Imaginer un nouveau western seulement un ou deux ans après GTA 6 supposerait donc que son développement ait déjà considérablement avancé en parallèle. Ce qui reste parfaitement possible, mais absolument pas démontré.
L'avenir de la licence paraît néanmoins moins incertain que sa date de sortie. Dès 2021, Strauss Zelnick , PDG de Take-Two , expliquait que des franchises comme GTA et Red Dead pouvaient perdurer très longtemps, à condition de maintenir leur qualité. Le retour de Red Dead paraît commercialement logique. Reste à savoir si Rockstar dispose réellement d'un troisième épisode suffisamment avancé pour viser 2028.

Activision se moque de Zelda : les chiffres ne mentent pas, Call of Duty est le challenger de GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Pour l'éditeur américain, Call of Duty : Modern Warfare 4 s'imposera aux côtés de GTA 6 comme l'un des deux véritables mastodontes de l'industrie, reléguant le retour de Link au second plan. Face au rouleau compresseur 6 prévu pour la mi-novembre, la grande majorité des éditeurs...
articles.txt:
Pour l'éditeur américain, Call of Duty : Modern Warfare 4 s'imposera aux côtés de GTA 6 comme l'un des deux véritables mastodontes de l'industrie, reléguant le retour de Link au second plan.
Face au rouleau compresseur 6 prévu pour la mi-novembre, la grande majorité des éditeurs ont préféré battre en retraite et décaler leurs lancements. Nintendo, de son côté, maintient le cap en sortant le remake très attendu de son classique Zelda Ocarina Of Time sur Switch 2, à peine deux semaines avant ce raz-de-marée. C'est dans ce climat particulièrement tendu que les responsables de la franchise Call Of Duty ont décidé de s'inviter dans le face-à-face, revendiquant haut et fort leur place au sommet.
Le positionnement de la célèbre licence s'est précisé lors d'une récente prise de parole stratégique. Interrogé sur l'attention médiatique massive captée par le duel entre Rockstar et Nintendo, Tyler Bahl, le directeur marketing d'Activision, a tenu à recadrer les débats :
Sans vouloir offenser Zelda, je pense que GTA 6 et Modern Warfare 4 sont les deux plus grands jeux de l'année . Le fait que davantage de personnes retournent sur les interfaces de leur console, dépoussièrent leur Xbox ou leur PlayStation et recommencent à jouer, va générer une plus grande audience pour nous de manière globale.
La logique de l'exécutif repose sur un phénomène d'aspiration : l'effervescence générée par GTA 6 attirera un flux massif de joueurs inactifs, qui graviteront ensuite naturellement vers les expériences multijoueurs compétitives. L'ADN social du jeu d'action reste, d'après lui, son argument le plus persuasif grâce à la possibilité de se retrouver entre amis sur une multitude de supports, incluant désormais la Switch 2.
Si le discours officiel se veut d'une assurance inébranlable, les analystes du secteur observent une réalité statistique légèrement plus contrastée. Les données mesurant l'intention d'achat aux États-Unis au mois d'août dernier illustrent bien le rapport de force actuel. L'engouement pour le prochain Call Of Duty s'élevait à 15 % auprès des joueurs sur PC et consoles de salon, tandis que le retour de Link affichait un score de 10,4 %.
Cet écart numérique brut masque cependant une disparité fondamentale en matière de matériel disponible. Les consoles de la génération actuelle de Sony et Microsoft, associées au parc PC, constituent un vivier gigantesque approchant les 50 millions d'utilisateurs sur le seul territoire américain. À l'inverse, la base installée de la Switch 2 n'atteint pas encore le cap des 7 millions de foyers. Proportionnellement au nombre d'acheteurs potentiels équipés du support adéquat, le taux d'adoption anticipé pour Zelda Ocarina Of Time s'avère donc considérablement plus intense.
Derrière cette confiance affichée face à Zelda et GTA, Activision traverse une période assez compliquée pour sa série phare. Les chiffres indépendants montrent une baisse progressive du nombre de joueurs réguliers de Call of Duty au cours des deux dernières années, passant de 40 millions à environ 25 millions par mois. Sur le plan commercial, Call of Duty : Black Ops 7 n'a d'ailleurs atteint que la cinquième place des meilleures ventes américaines, une vraie déception pour un jeu historiquement habitué à la première marche du podium.
L'arrivée de Modern Warfare 4 sur la nouvelle console de Nintendo représente donc un vrai moteur de croissance pour Activision. Cette opération s'accompagne d'un partenariat important entre les deux entreprises, pensé pour arranger tout le monde. Tyler Bahl ajoute à propos de cette alliance :
Nintendo s'est investi à fond. Nous avons lancé une campagne de co-marketing avec eux . À bien des égards, ils cherchent à vieillir leur clientèle et à toucher un public plus large en proposant un jeu de Call Of Duty sur leur machine. Les ventes de leur console ont augmenté jusqu'à un certain point avant de stagner, et cela leur permettra d'élargir leur offre.
Ce partenariat historique marque un tournant pour les deux géants. En unissant leurs forces, Activision et Nintendo espèrent ainsi attirer de nouveaux publics pour s'imposer face à la déferlante GTA 6 en cette fin d'année 2026.

articles.t: Sounds Like GTA 6 Will Be Full of Details Like Red Dead's Infamous Horse Balls
articles.chapeau: A decade of silence, finally broken
articles.txt:
Fans have spent years gossiping about a crass detail in Red Dead Redemption 2 that has never been officially acknowledged by developer Rockstar Games. That silence, alongside unclear video footage, made some gamers doubt the detail was truly an intended part of the game. Now, nearly a decade later, Rockstar has confirmed the existence of RDR2 's "horse balls" — and given players a good reason to believe Grand Theft Auto 6 will be full of similar flourishes.
The news comes via a YouTube video from Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier, who recently reported a major GTA 6 cover story for the outlet. The video is a summation of many notes that didn't make it into the final story, like an anecdote about how Rockstar spent years trying to redesign GTA 6 's weapon wheel. At one point, Rockstar got rid of the weapon wheel altogether. Yet despite countless iterations on the weapon loadout mechanic, Rockstar reverted to the original weapon wheel visible in GTA 6 footage.
The most surprising revelation, however, has to be about RDR2 's so-called horse balls. About nine years ago, footage of the open-world western went viral after fans noticed a strange animation. It seemed like Arthur Morgan's trusty steed had testicles with their own dedicated physics. Some swore that it looked like the stallion's privates would actually change shape depending on the weather.
Despite years of arguments, Rockstar never commented on the controversial feature. According to Schreier, the feature is real — but it was never a planned bullet point on Rockstar's production schedule. Instead, the animations made it into the final game because someone decided to spend time on it of their own accord. Schreier doesn't specify if the horse auteur was a single person or perhaps a group of people, but he did assert that RDR2 's long gestation period — and Rockstar parent company Take-Two's deep pockets — saw developers getting creative with what they put into the game.
"I think there are going to be a lot of details like that within this game," Schreier mused of GTA 6 while discussing RDR2 's horse balls.
GTA 6 isn't out yet, but Schreier's speculation is already well-substantiated. The open-world shooter is rife with minor details, like mud physics and complex NPC dialogue systems that showcase just how deep into the weeds Rockstar is willing to go. Whatever Rockstar did to craft its bespoke horse balls may well be getting an upgrade as well. Recent leaked footage showing co-protagonist Jason Duvall in the nude had viewers pointing out that the character's genitals had their own physics. We don't yet know if players will be able to move their members freely, but the game does feature a nudist colony where such physics would make perfect sense.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X on Nov. 19.

articles.chapeau: Le récent trailer de lancement de GTA 6 dévoile des graphismes exceptionnels mais fait l'impasse sur la nouvelle technologie de mise à l'échelle de Sony. Les analyses techniques confirment un rendu na
articles.txt:
Lire sur mobile Le récent trailer de lancement de GTA 6 dévoile des graphismes exceptionnels mais fait l'impasse sur la nouvelle technologie de mise à l'échelle de Sony. Les analyses techniques confirment un rendu natif en 1440p sans cette aide logicielle, jugée trop gourmande en ressources, tandis que le duo électro français Justice s'occupe d'une bande-son qui s'annonce déjà monumentale. Le célèbre studio américain a récemment dévoilé une séquence de 90 secondes de GTA 6, confirmant une sortie attendue pour le 19 novembre. Si la qualité visuelle globale impressionne par sa densité, l'analyse minutieuse des images capturées sur console révèle une approche technique très conservatrice. L'outil d'amélioration d'image par intelligence artificielle pourtant très vanté par Sony est totalement absent du flux vidéo. En parallèle de cette curiosité visuelle, la firme officialise une collaboration musicale d'envergure pour rythmer l'aventure de ses millions de futurs joueurs.
Les experts s'attendaient à voir la puissance logicielle qu QSR de Sony en action dès les premières secondes. Pourtant, le traitement d'image par QSSR (une technique d'upscaling propulsée par intelligence artificielle) brille par son absence. Sur la PS5 , ce silence technologique intrigue d'autant plus que le constructeur vante activement les mérites de cette fonctionnalité à tout va. Il semble que la gourmandise de cet algorithme refroidisse pourtant certains studios tiers.
Avec un objectif d'affichage fixé en 1440p natif, le moteur graphique monopolise déjà l'essentiel des capacités de calcul. Intégrer cet outil complexe coûterait environ 4 millisecondes sur un budget total de 33 ms, ce qui représente un sacrifice bien trop lourd pour un bénéfice marginal à l'écran. Les équipes de conception ont préféré allouer ces précieuses ressources à la physique du jeu et aux détails des décors. Il faut dire que GTA 6 s'annonce comme un monde ouvert qui fourmille de détails, il faut donc chercher l'optimisation au maximum.
Les précédentes vidéos promotionnelles avaient laissé les puristes sur leur faim avec d'étranges saccades dans les déplacements. Un rythme d'animation parfois hasardeux entachait la perception globale de l'œuvre. Sur ce nouveau montage de Grand Theft Auto VI , ces défauts du moteur interne semblent enfin appartenir au passé. Les mouvements respirent avec beaucoup plus de naturel.
Let's analyze tonemapping in GTA 6! Launch trailer is SDR but still gives us insight into how they are working with colors. Overall, what I see looks nice. Nothing appears particularly broken with one big exception. Gradients are smooth. Skin tones are great. Hue paths/shifts… pic.twitter.com/Kzlhd3agfO
La fluidité des déplacements des foules est désormais irréprochable. Même lors des lents panoramiques d'ambiance ou des scènes d'action frénétiques , le rendu global reste parfaitement cohérent. L'attente prolongée valait visiblement le coup pour peaufiner l'optimisation visuelle . C'est un soulagement majeur pour les joueurs qui redoutaient de retrouver les vieilles tares techniques des précédents épisodes.
La dimension sonore de cette aventure n'a pas été reléguée au second plan, bien au contraire. Le groupe électro emblématique Justice prend officiellement la direction de la partition originale. Leur premier extrait dévoilé, fusionnant les talents d'artistes internationaux prestigieux, garantit une ambiance urbaine électrique .
Le panorama musical s'annonce d'une richesse intense avec au total 34 morceaux exclusifs intégrés à la tracklist de lancement. Entre stations de radio virtuelles finement curatées et compositions instrumentales, le travail d'habillage sonore s'annonce pharaonique.
Les analyses techniques de la vidéo pointent vers une résolution de base en 1440p. L'image est ensuite étirée vers la 4K sans utiliser les derniers algorithmes de mise à l'échelle par intelligence artificielle de la console.
Le lancement mondial de l'aventure est programmé pour le 19 novembre sur les plateformes de salon actuelles, marquant le point culminant d'une attente longue de plus d'une décennie.
