GTA 6 : le dirigeable Goodyear survole Vice City dans une nouvelle publication officielle 19-10-2026 18:20 DL GAMING
Le compte Instagram officiel du Goodyear Blimp a publié un message faisant référence à Vice City, la célèbre ville fictive de l’univers Grand Theft Auto. Avec la mention Vice City, Leonida, USA, accompagnée des emojis plage et crocodile ainsi que du hashtag GTA 6, cette publication joue directement avec l’univers du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games.
La publication a été partagée sur le compte vérifié @goodyearblimp, consacré au célèbre dirigeable publicitaire Goodyear. Son message est volontairement concis : une localisation fictive, Vice City, associée à Leonida, l’État dans lequel se déroule GTA 6, et une référence explicite au jeu.
Le clin d’œil est particulièrement parlant pour les fans de la franchise. Vice City constitue l’un des lieux emblématiques de Grand Theft Auto et revient au premier plan dans le prochain épisode de Rockstar Games. L’association avec Leonida reprend directement les noms utilisés pour présenter l’environnement de GTA 6.
Avec GTA 6, Rockstar Games emmène les joueurs dans l’État fictif de Leonida, qui accueille notamment Vice City. Cette dernière s’inspire de Miami et de la Floride, avec un univers marqué par les paysages côtiers, les zones urbaines et les marécages.
Les crocodiles et l’ambiance balnéaire évoqués dans la publication de Goodyear font ainsi écho à l’imagerie associée à cette région. Le message adopte les codes visuels et géographiques de GTA 6 pour proposer un clin d’œil immédiatement reconnaissable par la communauté.
En associant le nom de Vice City à celui de Leonida, le compte officiel du Goodyear Blimp s’inscrit dans la vague de références à l’univers du prochain Grand Theft Auto. Une publication courte, mais suffisamment explicite pour attirer l’attention des fans et rappeler l’attente qui entoure le jeu.
Reste à savoir si ce clin d’œil se limitera aux réseaux sociaux ou s’il s’inscrit dans une initiative plus large.

articles.t: 13 Years Ago, Rockstar Suffered a Leak Worse Than GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Before unauthorized clips of GTA 6 scandalized fans, GTA 5 made video game leak history for Rockstar and Sony
articles.txt:
What could possibly be worse than footage of the world's most anticipated video game leaking onto the internet early , in an unfinished state? Easy. A game with a similar cultural footprint becoming playable ahead of its release. It seems unthinkable now in the age of Denuvo, but this exact nightmare scenario happened for Rockstar ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto 5 .
The leaks began a few weeks before GTA 5 's official launch, after a snafu with the PlayStation Store allowed players with pre-orders to access some of the game's files. At first, the leaks didn't seem like such a big deal. The files told fans how much space the game would take up on their PS3 hard drives, and listed specific songs from the game's soundtrack. Another leak stemming from early strategy guides also showed players the game's map sooner than intended.
To be sure, the leaks didn't make anyone working on the game happy. A blog post from Rockstar said , “As you can imagine, we are deeply disappointed by leaks and spoilers being spread in advance of the game's launch. GTA V represents years of hard work by many people across the world, and we all couldn't be more excited to finally share it with you properly this September 17th.”
Sony, for its part, subsequently pulled the preload and apologized profusely to fans and Rockstar for the gaffe. Compared to the GTA 6 leaks, where players were able to see the main characters naked, this data breach sounds quaint. It's less common these days, but there are plenty of modern examples of major games being pirated early. Heck, nearly every big Nintendo game of the last generation was pirated well ahead of launch.
Back in 2013, however, digital games had just entered the mainstream — and leaks of this magnitude weren't a regular occurrence. The situation worsened quickly after players began sharing information about the game's story and ending. Rockstar and Sony alike had to warn players that they could be banned for spoiling the game early. While we've seen glimpses of GTA 6 's story and have some educated guesses about its ending , Rockstar has managed to keep such details under wraps so far.
Image: Rockstar Games None of these events were nearly as significant as what came after: the game was uploaded to torrent websites. This leak subsequently allowed people with jailbroken consoles to play the game early without paying for it. Can you imagine the chaos that would unfold if the same happened in GTA 6 ? A leaker merely threatening to release GTA 6 early has been called a "doomsday scenario."
The circumstances are wildly different, of course. The game that leaked in 2013 was, as far as anyone could tell, the finished experience — and it was pirated somewhat close to launch. The GTA 6 that's ostensibly being held hostage by Cyberleek may be an old build with accompanying dev tools. Rockstar doesn't plan on releasing GTA 6 on a physical disc , and it's unclear if the PC version will only be streamable. The consequences of a GTA 6 leak where players could poke at the game's files and see how the sausage was made are hard to predict.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.
Phones and cameras also weren't nearly as good as they are now, so many of the leaks were shared in tiny, grainy pictures that were sometimes hard to make out.
"I don't know how 240p video even exists," one NeoGAF user complained .
Half of these leaks occurred on Vine, which doesn't even exist anymore. Meanwhile, GTA 6 's leaks show the protagonists fully nude in 4K .
Lucia Caminos using a punching bag in Grand Theft Auto 6 Rockstar Games/Take Two Interactive Some things are true in 2026 as they were in 2013, though. Years before they marveled at digital mud , fans couldn't believe how realistic GTA 5 looked.
"This could almost be a real live video footage," one Redditor remarked .
Most of all, nearly everyone hated watching the way other people played GTA. Either leakers are cursed to be bad video game players ... or no one is as good at GTA as they think.
"The dude was driving like an idiot," another NeoGAF user wrote .

articles.t: Cyberleek Threatens GTA 6 Build Leak Over Discs And An Apology
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek says a GTA 6 build leak will happen at a 30M market cap unless Take-Two ships physical discs and apologises. We look at what’s actually known.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 has spent years being picked apart by leakers, and now one of them is threatening to go much further than just sharing footage. Cyberleek has said on his website that he’ll release a playable build of the game to the public once he hits 30 million in market cap, as spotted in a post on r/GamingLeaksAndRumours . This GTA 6 build leak threat comes with conditions attached, and TakeTwo is the one being asked to meet them.
It is worth noting that none of this has been verified and there’s no confirmation that Cyberleek actually has a build, and neither Rockstar nor TakeTwo has responded publicly.
Cyberleek also acknowledged that the publisher probably assumes he’s bluffing and that’s a fair assumption on TakeTwo’s part, given that he hasn’t shown anything publicly that proves he has a build to release.
The market cap part is the strangest element. Market capitalisation usually refers to the total value of a company’s shares or a cryptocurrency token, but the post doesn’t say what asset this figure applies to, what currency it’s measured in or who controls it. Without that, it’s impossible to tell how close he is to the target, or whether the whole thing’s tied to some kind of token promotion.
The physical disc condition suggests Cyberleek is positioning himself as speaking for players rather than simply holding a game to ransom. The post doesn’t explain the reasoning, though, or what TakeTwo has done that he thinks warrants an apology.
Disc ownership has been a sore point across the industry for a while. More big releases are shipping as download codes or with only part of the game on the disc, and plenty of players see a physical copy as the only version they truly own. Whether that’s what’s driving this demand isn’t clear from what’s been shared.
If Cyberleek is bluffing, he’s picked a target where leaks are easy to believe. Rockstar’s history includes the 2022 breach that put early GTA 6 development footage online, and the hacker behind that is set to go back to court just days before the game launches . Older material keeps surfacing too, with stolen GTA 5 files revealing cancelled single-player expansions .
There’s a big difference between leaking video and leaking a working build, though. Footage spoils surprises. A build in the wild could be datamined for every mission, map area and system Rockstar’s spent years developing, and it’d give cheat makers a head start before the game even goes on sale.
For anyone on PC hoping a leak means getting hands on GTA 6 early, it’s worth being sceptical. Supposed leaked builds of huge games are a common lure for malware, because people are willing to download large archives from unknown sources and run whatever’s inside.
Even if a genuine build did appear, there’s no indication of what platform it’d be for or how complete it’d be. Development builds are often unstable, unoptimised and tied to specific hardware or tools, so it’s far from guaranteed anyone could run one on a normal gaming PC.
If something does surface claiming to be GTA 6, the safest move is to leave it alone. A compromised system isn’t a fair trade for an early look at a game that’s coming anyway. For now, this looks more like an attention grab than a credible threat, especially with that unexplained market cap target attached.
Do you think Cyberleek actually has a build, or is this a bluff aimed at hype? Let’s know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.t: GTA 6 : une carte collector serait incluse dans les éditions physiques
articles.chapeau: Une affiche repérée dans un magasin GameStop affirme que les versions physiques de GTA 6 incluront une carte collector. Rien d’officiel pour l’instant.
articles.txt:
Une affiche repérée dans un magasin GameStop affirme que les versions physiques de GTA 6 incluront une carte collector. Rien d’officiel pour l’instant.
Le plus important, là, c’est simple. Une nouvelle fuite autour de GTA 6 affirme qu’une carte collector physique serait glissée dans chaque copie physique du jeu. Sauf qu’on ne l’a pas vue, et personne n’a encore validé ça noir sur blanc.
Ce qui circule en ligne ne montre pas la carte elle-même. Juste son existence supposée. L’idée, c’est que les éditions physiques de GTA 6 incluraient une carte collector, ce qui parle forcément aux joueurs qui aiment les bonus tangibles, ceux qu’on garde après avoir refermé la boîte.
Mais il y a un vrai trou dans l’histoire. On ne sait pas à quoi ressemble cette carte, ni ce qu’elle contient exactement. Pas de visuel, pas de détail, pas de confirmation. Résultat ? Pour l’instant, c’est une info qui excite pas mal de monde, mais qui reste très incomplète.
L’origine de la fuite est assez précise. Un post apparu sur le Reddit consacré à GTA 6 montre ce qui ressemble à une publicité bricolée, affichée sur la vitrine d’un magasin GameStop . Le lieu exact du magasin n’a pas été révélé.
Ensuite, la machine s’est emballée. Le post a été repris par des comptes bien connus de la sphère Grand Theft Auto sur X et ailleurs, ce qui a suffi à faire remonter l’info très vite.
Le détail qui change un peu la donne, c’est que la personne ayant partagé le post dit être entrée dans le magasin et avoir parlé aux employés. D’après elle, ils auraient répété la même information. C’est intéressant, clairement. Ce n’est toujours pas une preuve définitive.
Ni GameStop ni qui que ce soit d’officiel n’a communiqué là-dessus. Et ça, ça pèse lourd. L’information aurait seulement fait surface dans certains magasins, pas via une annonce large et carrée.
Bon, on a donc une fuite plausible, un support physique aperçu en boutique, et un relais massif sur les réseaux. Mais on n’a pas la pièce maîtresse, une confirmation officielle. Tant qu’elle n’arrive pas, cette histoire de carte collector reste un bonus possible, pas une promesse gravée dans le marbre.
Pour les fans de GTA 6 , ça suffit à surveiller le dossier de près. Pas à précommander les yeux fermés.

articles.t: GTA 6 is eyeing Lucia as the next Arthur Morgan; here's why
articles.chapeau: Rockstar Games believes the new GTA heroine will 'stand tall' as the greatest gaming character ever created!
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games believes the new GTA heroine will 'stand tall' as the greatest gaming character they've ever created.
Taking over the mantle from Trevor, Franklin and Michael, the power duo of Lucia and Jason are quickly being examined by every Grand Theft Auto fan, as the Bonnie and Clyde protagonists hold the key to GTA 6 being the greatest game of all time.
Already, the two lead characters are kicking up a fuss, as the motivations behind their actions are being subjected to wild theories .
But Rockstar is going all in on framing the duo as a powerhouse team, as seen in the launch trailer , which was released on October 15.
In a frantic 90-second, action-heavy clip, the trailer consistently showcased Lucia's standalone personality, split only by steamy shower scenes that confirmed that the nude gameplay leaks were true.
With the new heroine set to take control of the GTA 6 narrative, Lucia is now being tipped to be the outright main character, and Rockstar is already putting her on a podium of the highest expectations.
Having championed a number of protagonists in a portfolio of colossal games, Rockstar Games has revealed that Lucia is their number one choice to be the face of the studio for the next generation, taking over from Arthur Morgan.
Of course, that's high praise, as Morgan is widely considered to be one of the best characters ever made, possibly the single greatest video game protagonist outside the likes of Nintendo's Mario.
At the very least, Morgan is regarded as the best of Rockstar Games, and that bar is set to be raised by Lucia,
Speaking in an interview with LOVE Magazine , Rockstar Games writer Alexa D'Agostino claimed that Lucia is the main driving force behind a lot of the decisions made in the storyline, often being overly naive, fearless and ambitious.
"Lucia had to be someone who wanted a better life for herself, and wouldn’t let the obstacles in the way of that life stop her getting it," she said.
"There are many badass women like her, just as there are many men like Jason. We just focused on capturing that.
"When you are focusing on writing a fully realized person with their own wants, you’re getting to get something perfectly imperfect, with clichés, but also undeniably real. That’s how you get a woman that can stand tall next to the likes of Arthur Morgan and Niko Bellic."
Read Next: GTA 6 leaker threatens to drop entire game as 6 new features confirmed in Lucia gameplay
Even the inclusion of Niko Bellic is an extremely high bar, as the Grand Theft Auto IV legend is often hailed as the pinnacle of the franchise, having been awarded a bigger role than the GTA V trio who shared responsibilities.
If we're projecting expectations, even matching John Marston from the original Red Dead Redemption would be enough for Lucia to spearhead GTA 6 to its perch as the greatest game of all time, leaving Jason to tip it over the edge.
The worry is that Jason's personality is rather bland, though, following his partner in crime at every turn, rather than having his own leads - that is, unless the popular dual-personality theory comes true...
Still, Lucia is the queen we'll be following moving forward, and if she's anything like what Rockstar is claiming, we're in for a huge treat.

articles.t: GTA 6 Trailer Features Meme Coin—And Solana Copycat Soars 2,900%
articles.chapeau: Rockstar released the launch trailer for GTA VI, revealing a potential meme coin in the upcoming game and sending degens wild.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 Trailer Features Meme Coin—And Solana Copycat Soars 2,900% Ryan Gladwin Fri, October 16, 2026 at 5:16 AM CDT 4 min read SOL-USD -1.18% PUMP36507-USD -1.79% Two seconds of the Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer was all it took for a Solana meme coin to fly, making some traders pretty rich.
Dacity Coin was seen plastered along the side of a plane in the GTA 6 launch trailer released on Thursday, with a man setting off a neon pink flare on the wing. This prompted a real meme coin of the same name to skyrocket 2,900% from a $104,000 market capitalization to $3.18 million, in the hour following the trailer's release.
Interestingly, the token had been created five days prior, after notorious Rockstar hacker "Cyberleek" leaked GTA 6 gameplay revealing that Dacity Coin was set to be in the game—but only a comparatively small group of traders noticed.
Upon its October 11 launch on Solana launchpad Pump.fun , Dacity Coin hit a peak market cap of $1.14 million before falling to $144,700 over the coming day and trading sideways until Thursday's sharp rise.
As a result, traders had plenty of time to buy into the meme coin before it skyrocketed. According to DEX Screener, 24 traders profited more than $10,000 on the token, with the top trader turning $1,912 into $44,000.
Dacity now sits at a $1.5 million market cap, dropping around 53% from its $3.18 million peak.
In the launch trailer, the plane reads "DacityCoin AudaCity," and in previously leaked footage, the game's protagonist Lucia can be seen skydiving wearing an AudaCity parachute. When the parachute opens, per the leaked screenshots, it features the slogan "Quit your job. Sell your house. Move [ineligible]."
According to the GTA wiki, Lucia is asked to parachute as a stunt to advertise the AudaCity brand and attract investment to the Dacity Coin.
If true, the game appears to be satirizing the stunts that meme coin creators have performed to promote their tokens over the years. In 2024, Decrypt reported that a man set himself on fire to promote his meme coin while others smoked drugs on livestream, pretended to be a dog, or recklessly shot a pistol out of their window.
This falls on the backdrop of years-long rumours of cryptocurrencies featuring in GTA 6. Several theories were thrown out, including play-to-earn features, NFT-owned properties, and even an entire blockchain for the game. However, all of them were unsubstantiated—Dacity Coin is the first solid sign of cryptocurrency being in the upcoming game.
How prominent will Dacity Coin be in the upcoming GTA 6 game? That's the question currently on the lips of traders. If it's a mainstay of the game, then degens might stand to profit handsomely from holding the token for longer. If not, well, this might be the end of the road.
In February 2025, Fortnite added a fake crypto coin called Dill Bits, and degens quickly launched a real one on Solana that hit a $4.78 million market cap before crashing 96%. It pumped 2,700% again in April after Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a scam , then dropped 82% within days.
"I didn't launch it. What is wrong with you people," Sweeney posted, as traders floated theories that he was secretly behind the coin.
The Dill Bits community took the whole thing as bullish, given that Fortnite's storyline was literally about a pickle villain called Big Dill running a crypto rug pull. It didn't help much, with DB dropping 82.3% in the days that followed.
Epic Games told Decrypt at the time that there was "no real cryptocurrency or memecoin associated with Fortnite or endorsed by Epic."
Rockstar has yet to say anything about Dacity Coin, and the game studio did not respond to Decrypt 's request for comment.

A few days later, the leaker said they wouldn't leak GTA 6's ending if Take-Two left them alone.
On August 18, an unidentified person or group going by the name "Cyberleek" began sharing what appeared to be Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips on the internet.
The internet was naturally skeptical, but the footage was hard to fault: It looked authentic, showing mundane GTA 6 gameplay featuring its male protagonist, Jason. In one clip the player shot a basketball outside of the same house we've seen in the trailers, and in another he did some typical GTA random-civilian-murdering.
A day later, Cyberleek dropped two more videos , both of which also looked legit. At the same time, the clips were being stricken from social media on copyright grounds—the only public response from Take-Two and Rockstar so far.
The fifth video Cyberleek released ended with a twist: the player writing the word "LEEK" into the side of a building with bullet holes. These are not, it turns out, clips taken by GTA 6 testers and found on an unsecured server, as many assumed. Cyberleek has (or had) access to a build of GTA 6 , or a portion of it.
We don't know exactly how Cyberleek is getting their clips. The footage of them shooting "LEEK" into a wall indicates they have or had access to a playable build, but it is not necessarily the full game. It's notable that GTA 6's other protagonist, Lucia, has not shown up in the clips.
It does seem that these clips are from a relatively recent build, however. In one of the clips, the in-game radio is playing "Sports Car" by Tate McRae, which released in January 2025.

Cyberleek has made common consumer rights complaints their justification for the leaks: "Publishers sell licenses and call them purchases. They ship unfinished games and call them living services. They lock content on discs and call it DLC. They kill games and keep the money. Every year anti-consumerism tightens its grip, and every year gamers get less for what they pay."
At a glance, Cyberleek's complaints seem typical, but two of the three demands they've put forward strike me as slightly strange choices.
The demands are: no more digital preorders, no more selling DLC already contained in the base game files, and mandatory "offline fallback states" for the singleplayer components of games.
The third demand is the most expected, and is similar though not identical to the demand of the Stop Killing Games movement (which has disavowed the leaker ).
The other two, however, don't seem like the kind of core issues most people would choose if they were putting forward their three biggest gripes about the games industry in 2026.
On-disc DLC—where add-on content is included in the base game's files, but inaccessible without paying extra—was a big controversy around 10-15 years ago, but is much less relevant in today's mostly discless world.
The complaint that preorders don't really mean anything when you're not preordering an actual physical disc is also valid, but seems like a roundabout way to complain about the heart of the issue: The end of physical media, which has been a hot button topic following Sony's announcement that it will cease disc production .
I'm not sure you can rally a movement behind ending digital preorder bonuses and preloading: GTA 6 itself has already enjoyed an "unprecedented" number of preorders . You can definitely rally a movement behind seeing more GTA 6 leaks, though.
The leaker is promoting the $Cyberleek token alongside the leaks—the market cap is $1.1M at the time of writing—and claims that the funds will go toward "a secret project."
For now, the tokens are being used to vote in polls that determine the next clip to be released. The most recent clip , a flyover of Vice City, was the winner of a vote.

L’affaire Cyberleek connaît un nouveau rebondissement. Alors que le responsable présumé des nombreuses fuites de GTA 6 annonçait mettre fin à ses publications, un nouveau message vient contredire cette décision.
Sur son site, Cyberleek affiche désormais une annonce intitulée “DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT”. Il affirme proposer une version de développement du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games pour 40 dollars. Cette nouvelle déclaration intervient quelques heures seulement après son message The End of t he Road , dans lequel il expliquait renoncer à diffuser sa prétendue build complète.
Depuis plusieurs jours, Cyberleek conditionnait la publication d’une version jouable de GTA 6 à un objectif financier. Sa cryptomonnaie devait atteindre une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars. Cet objectif n’a pas été atteint.
Dans son message du 14 octobre, l’entité expliquait donc qu’elle ne publierait pas la build, évoquant notamment les risques associés à la distribution anonyme de plus de 200 Go de données. Mais quelques heures plus tard, changement de discours.
Le site affiche désormais une annonce concernant une version baptisée, GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025. Cyberleek décide de la proposer mais réclame directement 40 dollars pour accéder au téléchargement.
C’est évidemment la grande question. Cyberleek affirme depuis plusieurs semaines disposer d’une version suffisamment complète pour parcourir l’intégralité de la campagne solo. Les nombreuses vidéos diffusées depuis août suggèrent aussi un accès à des contenus de développement du jeu.
Mais tout ceci n’est pas suffisant pour confirmer qu’il s’agit bien ici d’une version complète de GTA 6. De plus aucun chercheur en sécurité ni média spécialisé n’a confirmé avoir exécuté et authentifié cette prétendue build.
La prudence est indispensable car des fichiers malveillants présentés comme des versions anticipées de GTA 6 ont déjà circulé sur Internet. GinjFo avait notamment signalé en août une fausse build dépassant 100 Go qui dissimulait un malware.
Nous déconseillons de payer ou de télécharger cette archive même si son contenu est vérifié indépendamment. Toute cette histoire repose sur un acte malveillant, de la piraterie et du chantage.

articles.chapeau: A new launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI reveals more details about what's set to be the biggest game of the year.
articles.txt:
Share Save Add as preferred on Google Laura Cress and Liv McMahon , Technology reporters Rockstar Games GTA 6 will feature Jason and Lucia as playable characters Rockstar has released a new launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, revealing more details about what is set to be the biggest game of the year.
GTA 6 became available to pre-order at midnight on 25 June in the UK and elsewhere around the world, after Rockstar revealed the game's pre-sales launch date and cover art in mid-June.
Analysts believe Rockstar's action adventure could become the most expensive game ever made, with estimates putting development costs at more than $1bn (£866m).
The new launch trailer again confirmed GTA 6 will be released on 19 November.
Suggesting no further delays to its release, the video gave fans a glimpse into the missions that protagonists Jason and Lucia will take part in.
It also featured a new song from French electronic music artists Justice, who were revealed to be the game's original score composers.
The game has been previously delayed twice , from autumn 2025 and May 2026.
In a statement when the second delay was announced, Rockstar said it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to "expect and deserve".
Rockstar said players who pre-order will be able to begin pre-loading it on their consoles on 12 November to ensure they are able to play at launch.
The sixth game in the main series will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.
There's no news on when a PC version will be released - it's also currently unknown whether it will come to Nintendo Switch 2.
The game will cost £69.99 in the UK and $79.99 in the US - with an ultimate edition, featuring extra vehicles and weapons, priced at £89.99 and $99.99, respectively.
Physical copies of the game will contain a code for a digital download for the game inside a box, rather than a disc.
Rockstar has not yet confirmed whether an updated online mode will be released as soon as GTA 6 launches.
The game's PlayStation Store listing currently states "Grand Theft Auto VI is a single-player experience" - implying there will be no online mode at launch. But given GTA Online's success , it will likely exist at some point.
How any future age verification legislation in the UK around social media and particularly messaging in gaming could therefore affect it, if at all, is still unknown.
GTA 6 will feature its first ever playable female protagonist in a 3D setting - Lucia - alongside her partner in life and crime, Jason, as a second playable character.
From what we've seen in two gameplay trailers and Netflix's extended look , the story will follow the pair in a Bonnie and Clyde-esque adventure through the seedy underbelly of America after an " easy score goes wrong ".
Like other GTA games before it, the sixth chapter is set in a fictional US state - this time in Leonida, which is Rockstar's version of Florida.
Fans of previous games will be excited to hear that Vice City, which is inspired by Miami, will return, featuring as the main city within the state.
GTA 6's cover art revealed by Rockstar on 18 June made several nods to the setting with alligators and flamingos.
It's no secret that GTA 6 has been a few years in the making.
The franchise's last instalment, GTA 5, was released in September 2013 - and quickly became one of the best-selling games of all time.
It's unclear whether Rockstar has been working on the sixth instalment for all of that time, however, as in 2018 it also released another huge sequel - Red Dead Redemption 2.
Rockstar confirmed for the first time that it was working on a sixth game in the series in February 2022.
The rising cost of development and immense pressure to live up to the series' hype are all contributing factors as to why gamers have had to wait so long for the game's release.
Several months later, footage and images leaked after teenage hackers targeted the company .
It has also seen some issues since, including accusations of "union-busting" by sacked workers at Rockstar North , its Edinburgh HQ, where developers have been racing to get GTA 6 ready for release in November.
To put it simply, the GTA franchise is one of the biggest and most profitable entertainment properties in history.
GTA 5 has sold nearly 230 million copies, making it one of the best-selling games of all time - which has generated billions of dollars in revenue for Rockstar.

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Threads Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Rockstar Games co-head of development Aaron Garbut says Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks from 2022 were an "invasive" moment The leaks caused a huge shift at Rockstar that forced a five-day in-office work policy for security reasons Rockstar’s head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, says Rockstar plans to reexamine the policy after GTA 6 launches Rockstar Games has addressed the initial Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks from 2022, calling it an "invasive" moment that resulted in a huge policy shift at the studio.
In a lengthy interview with Bloomberg , where Rockstar leadership discussed GTA 6 's long development period, co-head of development Aaron Garbut touched on the huge leaks from 2022 that changed how the studio works today.
In September of that year, someone hacked the company's Slack channel and leaked dozens of raw, unfinished gameplay footage before Rockstar was ready to unveil anything. Rockstar released a statement about the leaks, and despite copyright takedowns, the footage quickly spread like wildfire, and though law enforcement later tracked the alleged hacker down, it was too late.
"It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing," Garbut said. "It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level."
As a result, Rockstar introduced a controversial policy in 2024 requiring every developer to work in-office five days a week for security reasons; developers were also banned from accessing Rockstar’s servers and tools outside the office, which forced them to take vacation days if they needed to stay home for childcare or emergencies.
The policy set back the cultural progress the studio made after Red Dead Redemption 2 's release, a game made under extensive periods of "crunch." With GTA 6 , Rockstar knew it couldn't repeat those mistakes; however, the new policy following the leaks meant no more hybrid working.
Rockstar’s head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg, however, that the studio plans to reexamine the policy after GTA 6 launches, though she doubts it will be able to switch to the more common three-days-in, two-days-out hybrid work model.

Unfortunately, more leaks have since occurred, notably ahead of Rockstar's GTA 6 extended look , and persist to this day, with a prevalent leaker known as 'Cyberleek' threatening to release more in the lead-up to the game's launch on November 19.

Après une série de leaks concernant GTA 6, le hacker Cyberleek a déclaré avoir publié les derniers éléments disponibles sur le jeu. Comme il n’a pas réussi à atteindre son objectif, à savoir une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars pour le memecoin, les fans ne verront ni spoilers sur l’intrigue ni version complète du jeu sur PC.
Cette annonce s’est accompagnée d’un nouvel extrait vidéo de gameplay qui, selon l’auteur des leaks, contient des images des missions finales. La vidéo commence par une scène où Lucia se trouve dans un salon de coiffure.
Dans son dernier message, Cyberleek a d’abord tenté de justifier ses précédentes ventes de cryptomonnaie. Selon lui, tous les objectifs atteints jusqu’alors étaient liés à la publication des leaks de GTA 6 promis. L’auteur a toutefois accusé d’autres acteurs du marché des cryptomonnaies de l’avoir injustement rendu responsable de la « réaction en chaîne » des ventes de l’actif.
Cyberleek a également déclaré qu’il ne publierait pas de spoilers sur l’intrigue, car ceux-ci pourraient « gâcher l’expérience de jeu des joueurs qui n’ont rien fait de mal ». Selon lui, l’éditeur Take-Two a déjà subi une punition suffisante et il ne souhaite donc pas nuire davantage à l’entreprise.
La publication d’une version PC complète de plus de 200 Go aurait pu causer un préjudice encore plus important à Take-Two et Rockstar Games. Toutefois, sans atteindre l’objectif de 30 millions de dollars en cryptomonnaie, Cyberleek a décidé que le risque n’en valait pas la peine.
L’auteur a de nouveau souligné que les dons étaient un moyen de montrer son soutien, et non un investissement. Il a promis que « les leaks s’arrêtent ici. Du moins pour l’instant ». On ignore encore si Cyberleek recommencera à publier des éléments avant la sortie officielle de GTA 6.
Malgré cette annonce de la fin des leaks, les joueurs ont reçu une nouvelle vidéo de gameplay d’environ 4 minutes. La vidéo s’intitule « The End of the Road », tandis que la chanson « Don’t Stop Believin’ » de Journey retentit pendant tout l’enregistrement.
Cyberleek annonce la fin des leaks de GTA 6 après avoir publié le 20e extrait, mais affirme que le mécanisme de déclenchement différé est actif et que des spoilers sur l’intrigue, y compris la fin, seront publiés si Take-Two le retrouve :
“CL possède la fin. Elle a été envisagée. Elle punirait lourdement Take-Two, mais gâcherait l’expérience des joueurs qui n’ont rien fait de mal. Si on laisse CL tranquille, il ne se déclenchera jamais. Celui qui éliminera CL fera ce choix.
Les 30 millions n’ont pas été atteints, donc pas de build. Téléverser anonymement plus de 200 Go représente un risque sérieux – cela n’en valait la peine que si l’étape intermédiaire finançait le projet secret.

articles.t: Cyberleek Ends GTA 6 Leaks - Root-Nation.com
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek has announced the end of the GTA 6 leaks and refused to publish story spoilers or a PC build exceeding 200 GB.
articles.txt:
© ROOT-NATION.com - Use of content is permitted with a backlink.
After a series of GTA 6 leaks, hacker Cyberleek said that he had published the final materials related to the game. Since he failed to achieve his stated goal of pushing the memecoin’s market capitalization to $30 million, fans will see neither story spoilers nor a complete PC version of the game.
Another gameplay clip appeared alongside the announcement. According to the leaker, it contains footage from the final missions. The video begins with a scene in which Lucia is inside a barbershop.
In his latest message, Cyberleek initially tried to justify his previous cryptocurrency sales. According to him, all the goals achieved earlier were tied to publishing the promised GTA 6 leaks. At the same time, the leaker accused other participants in the cryptocurrency market of unfairly holding him responsible for the asset’s “chain reaction” of sales.
Cyberleek also said that he would not publish story spoilers because they could “ruin the experience for gamers who did nothing wrong.” In his view, publisher Take-Two had already been punished enough, so he did not want to cause the company any additional harm.
Publishing a complete PC version exceeding 200 GB could have caused Take-Two and Rockstar Games even more serious damage. However, without reaching the $30 million cryptocurrency goal, Cyberleek decided that the risk was not justified.
The leaker again emphasized that the donations were a way to show support, not an investment. He promised that “the leaks stop here. For now, at least.” It remains unknown whether Cyberleek will resume publishing materials before the official release of GTA 6.
Despite announcing the end of the leaks, players received another gameplay video lasting approximately four minutes. The video is titled “The End of the Road,” and Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’” plays throughout the recording.
Cyberleek announces the end of the GTA 6 leaks after posting the 20th clip, but says the dead man’s switch is active and story spoilers, including the ending, will be published if Take-Two catches him:
“CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin the experience for the gamers who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy – why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leak – clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. The dead man’s switch is active – story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it.
The 30M was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project.
Terms honored as written. Sad, the negativity – and how few believe anything real is behind this. CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an investment.
It changed nothing – influencers decided the story before the facts arrived. The Edict stands. The leaks stop here. For now.”
Lucia first enters a barbershop, where NPCs can be heard talking in the background. When Jason’s partner leaves the establishment, she hits the cashier and robs him.
A significant portion of the video focuses on changing hairstyles, after which the protagonist heads to a clothing store to purchase various items. The clip also shows a minigame that will presumably be available in GTA 6. During an episode resembling a mission, Lucia plays pool in a bar and receives a small amount of money for it.
Before the video ends, viewers see a cinematic shot of a bridge. Various locations in the fictional state of Leonida are shown next, after which the video switches to a residential area that, judging by its appearance, resembles a location outside Florida.

articles.chapeau: Le leaker CyberLeek suspend ses fuites sur GTA 6 après l’échec de son objectif crypto de 30 millions de dollars. Les spoilers restent une menace.
articles.txt:
Les joueurs qui attendent GTA 6 peuvent souffler, au moins temporairement. Le leaker connu sous le pseudonyme CyberLeek a annoncé le 14 octobre 2026 qu’il mettait fin à ses révélations sur le prochain jeu de Rockstar Games « pour le moment » . Son projet consistait notamment à publier une prétendue version jouable du titre si sa cryptomonnaie atteignait une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars. L’objectif n’a pas été atteint.
Cette annonce intervient alors que la sortie de GTA 6 est prévue le 19 novembre 2026 . Depuis plusieurs semaines, CyberLeek multipliait les révélations supposées sur le jeu, alimentant la curiosité des fans tout en menaçant de dévoiler des éléments majeurs de son scénario.
La prudence reste toutefois de mise. Le leaker affirme toujours détenir la fin du jeu et a déjà diffusé des extraits sortis de leur contexte concernant les dernières missions. Quant à la prétendue version jouable, rien ne permet de confirmer son existence ou son authenticité.
Dans un message intitulé « End of the Road » , publié le 14 octobre, CyberLeek a annoncé suspendre ses fuites. Le leaker explique notamment qu’il ne publiera pas la fin de GTA 6, affirmant vouloir éviter de gâcher l’expérience des joueurs qui n’ont rien fait de mal .
Cette déclaration intervient après l’échec de son objectif financier . CyberLeek avait conditionné la publication d’une prétendue version complète du jeu à une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars pour sa cryptomonnaie. Le seuil n’ayant pas été atteint, il affirme renoncer à cette publication.
Il convient néanmoins de distinguer les annonces du leaker des faits vérifiés. L’existence d’une version jouable complète de GTA 6 n’est pas établie. Les joueurs qui souhaitent découvrir GTA 6 sans connaître son intrigue ont donc intérêt à éviter les publications et discussions susceptibles de contenir des révélations.

Cette décision n’est pas une surprise puisqu’elle a été conditionnée à l’échec d’une opération liée à une cryptomonnaie. Le groupe voulait porter sa capitalisation à 30 millions de dollars , un seuil qui n’a pas été atteint.

articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the anonymous account behind months of Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, says it is done. On October 14, 2026, the leaker posted a three-part message titled “End of the road,” announcing it will not release a full game build, will not post the game’s ending, and does not plan further early gameplay leaks. The post marks the clearest signal yet that the long-running GTA 6 leak saga, which has rattled Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive for the better part of a year, may finally be winding down.
Whether that holds is a separate question. Cyberleek has reversed course before, and nothing in the latest message can be independently verified beyond the post itself. Still, the announcement reframes a leak campaign that previously threatened to dump an entire playable build onto torrent sites. Instead, the leaker is walking away, at least for now, while keeping a handful of final-mission clips online as what it calls proof of access.

According to the October 14 post, Cyberleek broke its farewell statement into three distinct parts. The first addressed the fate of the alleged full game build, the second covered the ending and story content, and the third offered a handful of final clips described as proof rather than spoilers. Kotaku reported on the message under the headline “GTA 6 Leaker Announces They Won’t Release The Full Game” , framing it as the leaker calling a stop to the campaign, at least for the time being.
Cyberleek had previously floated a conditional threat: if a crypto token tied to the account hit a $30 million market cap, the full build would go out, story mode included, all the way to the credits. In its own words from that earlier post, “Here’s the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out, full story mode, played to the end, credits and all,” as Gadgets360 reported at the time. That target was never reached, and the October 14 message closes the loop on it.
Cyberleek’s stated reasoning centers on risk versus reward. Uploading hundreds of gigabytes of a stolen build anonymously carries real exposure, and the leaker framed the payoff as only worth it if the crypto milestone had funded whatever project sat behind the threat. With the target missed, the math apparently stopped working. The account has made no claim about a PC build timeline, pricing, or file size beyond what it has already posted, and none of those specifics are confirmed by any outlet covering the story.
This is a notable shift from the tone Cyberleek struck in earlier posts, which read more like negotiation tactics aimed at Take-Two than a farewell. Eurogamer covered the escalation at the time the full-build threat first surfaced, and the contrast between that posture and the October 14 retreat is stark. Readers can track the earlier claim in shattered.io’s own coverage of Cyberleek’s 200GB “playable” build claim , which laid out the scope of what the leaker said it was holding.
The second part of the message dealt specifically with the game’s ending, and it’s arguably the most consequential piece of the whole statement. Cyberleek claims to have access to the conclusion of GTA 6’s story but says it will not publish it. In its own words, reported by Kotaku, “CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly, but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy, why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished.”

No outlet has confirmed whether the claimed ending footage actually exists, and Take-Two has not addressed the claim directly.

The leaker characterized them in its own words as “the latest leek, clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing,” according to Kotaku’s report. articles.txt:
Cyberleek a publié un flot continu de fuites sur GTA 6 , confrontant Rockstar à son pire cauchemar. Bien que l'auteur des fuites affirme avoir arrêté, le processus de test pourrait potentiellement révéler des spoilers. NateTheHate, une source fiable , a ensuite précisé que des exemplaires seront mis à disposition avant la fin du mois d'octobre. Cette nouvelle répond à certaines questions sur la manière dont le studio prévoit de gérer les tests de GTA 6 .

Comme la plupart des fans s’attendent à au moins 50 heures de jeu, confiner les journalistes n’aurait peut-être pas été envisageable. Au-delà de l’histoire et des missions principales, Leonida est plus vaste que tous les précédents mondes ouverts de Rockstar. Il semble désormais que les testeurs disposeront de 3 semaines ou plus pour explorer Vice City et ses environs.

articles.txt:
Le leaker anonyme qui diffuse depuis la mi-août des images d'une version de travail de GTA 6 vient d'annoncer la fin de sa campagne, sans publier le jeu complet. Quand il menaçait de diffuser le jeu entier , CyberLeek promettait la version jouable si la capitalisation de sa monnaie atteignait 30 millions de dollars. Take-Two pouvait, selon lui, éviter la fuite en sortant GTA 6 sur disque et en présentant des excuses publiques. Kotaku situait cette capitalisation autour de 2,2 millions de dollars le 12 octobre, après une chute de moitié en vingt-quatre heures, alors qu'elle avait dépassé 4,75 millions le week-end précédent. Le leaker reconnaît avoir vendu à deux reprises, en ne prélevant selon lui que des frais de transaction. Il rejette les accusations d'arnaque, qu'il attribue surtout à des youtubeurs. Le jeton était, répète-t-il, « un don, jamais un investissement ». Ceux qui avaient acheté le jeton dans l'espoir d'obtenir le jeu complet ne l'auront pas.
Avant de partir, CyberLeek a publié une dernière vidéo courte, qu'il présente comme des extraits des ultimes missions et que rien ne permet d'authentifier. Il affirme détenir la fin du jeu, mais dit renoncer à la publier parce qu'elle punirait Take-Two en gâchant l'expérience de joueurs « qui n'ont rien fait de mal ».
Le message se termine sur « The leeks stop here. For now. », soit « les fuites s'arrêtent ici, pour l'instant », avec le jeu de mots sur les poireaux (leeks) d'où vient son pseudonyme. CyberLeek prévient aussi qu'il garde des révélations sur l'histoire en réserve, qu'un mécanisme automatique mettrait en ligne si quelqu'un le faisait taire. La menace vise la traque judiciaire lancée par Take-Two, qui a réclamé des assignations à Discord, Microsoft, X et YouTube pour l'identifier. L'existence de ce dispositif automatique n'est pas établie. Les extraits diffusés en deux mois ne prouvent pas non plus que CyberLeek possède le jeu complet.
Rockstar n'a pas commenté ces dernières images. Le studio vient de retracer la genèse de GTA 6 pour Bloomberg , piratage de 2022 compris, en promettant que son prochain jeu ne demandera pas huit ans de travail.
L'ultimatum de CyberLeek sur le disque visait un vrai point faible, puisque les boîtes de GTA 6 ne contiendront qu'un code de téléchargement, comme le rappelle notre dossier sur la sortie . Il a surtout servi à faire monter le jeton. GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series. D'ici là, toute « version complète » proposée hors des boutiques officielles reste un piège.

articles.t: Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 40 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 lance de nouvelles menaces
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek menace de révéler la fin de GTA 6 s
articles.txt:
Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 40 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 lance de nouvelles menaces Luis Blanco mer. 14 octobre 2026 à 7:32 PM UTC−5 3 min de lecture TTWO Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 41 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 menace de révéler la fin. Photo by BeInCrypto Cyberleek, le leaker pseudonyme de GTA 6, affirme que la fin du jeu sera révélée s'il se fait attraper, une menace qui survient alors que le token lié à ses fuites dégringole.
Le token a chuté de 41 % mercredi, et la sortie de GTA 6 est désormais prévue dans environ cinq semaines.
Cyberleek a publié un dernier message ce matin, déclarant que la version complète restera privée. Le compte affirme posséder déjà la fin du jeu.
À titre de preuve, le compte a montré des extraits hors contexte des missions finales de l'histoire. Plutôt que de tout rendre public, le leaker propose un « dead man's switch » qui dévoilerait la fin s'il venait à être arrêté.
Le leaker estime que Take-Two, la maison-mère de Rockstar Games, a déjà assez souffert, et que la publication de spoilers nuirait à l'expérience des joueurs.
Le jeu est toujours prévu pour le 19 novembre. Chris Bratt, du média People Make Games, indique qu'un tribunal réunissant Rockstar et 34 employés licenciés se tiendra les 17 et 18 novembre.
Certains utilisateurs sur X spéculent que Cyberleek pourrait faire partie des employés licenciés, même si rien ne vient le confirmer. Cela dit, les extraits sont diffusés hors contexte, ce qui rend leur authenticité difficile à vérifier.
Le leaker publie du contenu inédit de GTA 6 et associe chaque nouvelle fuite à la valorisation du token CYBERLEEK. En effet, son prix détermine combien du jeu parvient jusqu'aux fans.
CYBERLEEK a chuté de 41 % en 24 heures et s'échange autour de 0,00155 $, selon les données de CoinGecko. Ce prix se situe environ 96 % en dessous de son record historique.
Des paliers de valorisation ont rythmé chaque publication depuis le début. Les premières fuites avaient propulsé le token jusqu'à 40 millions de dollars de capitalisation.
Le token a ensuite grimpé de 200 % en deux jours, sans toutefois retrouver ce pic initial. Cyberleek a alors décidé de ne plus publier l'intégralité du contenu. Sa capitalisation boursière dépasse à peine le million de dollars, très loin de l'objectif des 30 millions.
La feuille de route relie les prochaines fuites à l'atteinte de nouveaux paliers de plusieurs millions de dollars de capitalisation. Le leaker précise que les révélations régulières vont cesser, car le token performe mal.

articles.t: GTA 6 : le hacker Cyberleek met fin aux fuites et renonce à publier le jeu complet
articles.chapeau: Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l'arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu'il affirme détenir.
articles.txt:
Sony détaille un peu plus la rétrocompatibilité sur sa PlayStation 5. Il sera possible de jouer à la grande majorité des jeux PlayStation 4 sur la PS5, mais tous ne seront pas compatibles.
Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l’arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu’il affirme détenir . Dans un message publié aujourd’hui sur son site, le hacker explique que son objectif financier n’a pas été atteint, tout en laissant planer la possibilité de nouvelles révélations.
Dans un message en trois parties intitulé The End of the Road , Cyberleek confirme qu’il ne publiera pas la version jouable complète de GTA 6 qu’il prétend avoir en sa possession. Le hacker affirmait auparavant pouvoir diffuser l’intégralité du mode histoire, jusqu’au générique de fin, si sa cryptomonnaie atteignait 30 millions de dollars. Cet objectif n’ayant pas été atteint, la publication est annulée.
Cyberleek avance également un argument pratique : mettre en ligne anonymement un fichier de plus de 200 Go présenterait des risques importants, sans contrepartie financière suffisante. L’existence de cette version complète et sa taille restent toutefois non vérifiées. Aucun élément indépendant ne permet de confirmer que le pirate possède réellement une copie jouable intégrale du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games.
L’annonce intervient après plusieurs semaines de leaks d’extraits de gameplay issus d’une version de développement . Le leaker avait notamment publié une longue séquence montrant Jason et Lucia, les deux protagonistes, ainsi que différentes situations de jeu. Certaines images semblaient provenir de missions avancées de l’histoire.
Cyberleek affirme également connaître le dénouement du jeu, mais assure avoir choisi de ne pas le révéler afin de préserver l’expérience des joueurs. Il soutient que les dernières séquences publiées proviennent de missions finales, présentées sans leur contexte narratif pour éviter de dévoiler les principaux rebondissements.
Le message contient toutefois une réserve importante : « Les fuites s’arrêtent ici. Pour l’instant »/ Cyberleek affirme aussi avoir activé un mécanisme de publication différée qui déclencherait la diffusion de spoilers s’il était pris pour cible par les autorités. Cette menace entretient donc l’incertitude sur la suite de l’affaire, malgré l’annonce d’un arrêt des publications de leaks.
La campagne de Cyberleek associait les révélations sur GTA 6 à une cryptomonnaie portant son nom. En échange d’une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars, le leaker promettait de publier le jeu complet. Il avait également posé une autre condition à Take-Two, maison mère de Rockstar Games : sortir le jeu sur disque physique et présenter des excuses publiques. Pour rappel, Grand Theft Auto VI sera uniquement disponible en version numérique . Cyberleek rejette les accusations selon lesquelles cette opération aurait constitué une escroquerie destinée à faire monter artificiellement la valeur du token avant sa revente.
Rockstar Games n’a pas publiquement commenté cette dernière annonce. Sa maison mère, Take-Two, cherche néanmoins à identifier le ou les responsables des fuites, notamment au moyen de procédures judiciaires visant à obtenir des informations auprès de plateformes en ligne. Discord et Microsoft font partie des plateformes visées . La publication du jeu complet n’est donc plus à l’ordre du jour selon Cyberleek, mais rien ne garantit que les fuites cesseront définitivement avant la sortie officielle de GTA 6 , prévue le 19 novembre sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X/S.
Merci de nous avoir signalé l'erreur, nous allons corriger cela rapidement.

articles.t: GTA 6 : CyberLeek arrête ses activités et ne publiera plus aucun extrait
articles.txt:
Le groupe CyberLeek , connu pour avoir diffusé de nombreux extraits de GTA 6 avant sa sortie officielle, a annoncé la fin de ses activités. Cette décision intervient alors que l’intérêt pour les fuites s’est considérablement essoufflé, notamment depuis que Rockstar communique régulièrement sur le jeu. Les joueurs peuvent donc souffler : plus aucune image volée ne viendra gâcher la découverte du titre, attendu pour le 19 novembre 2026 .
CyberLeek ne se contentait pas de publier des fuites : le groupe avait également lancé sa propre cryptomonnaie , espérant tirer profit de la notoriété acquise grâce aux extraits de GTA 6 . Plus tôt dans la semaine, il avait fixé un objectif ambitieux : atteindre une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars . En échange, il promettait de diffuser l’intégralité du jeu, y compris sa fin. Mais le marché en a décidé autrement. La valeur de la cryptomonnaie a chuté de manière significative, passant sous la barre des 5 millions de dollars ces derniers jours. Face à cet échec, le groupe a préféré jeter l’éponge.
Dans un message relayé par Insider Gaming, CyberLeek a expliqué sa décision de ne pas diffuser la fin de GTA 6 . Le groupe affirme avoir envisagé cette option pour « punir » Take-Two, l’éditeur du jeu, mais a finalement renoncé. Selon ses propres mots : « CL (CYBERLEEKS) détient la fin [de GTA 6]. L’idée a été envisagée. Cela aurait puni considérablement Take-Two, mais ça aurait gâché l’expérience des joueurs, qui n’y étaient pour rien. Take-Two n’aurait fait preuve d’aucune clémence envers CL – pourquoi CL en ferait-il preuve ? Take-Two a déjà été suffisamment puni. La fin ne sera pas publiée. »
L’arrêt des activités de CyberLeek est aussi le signe que les fuites n’ont plus le même impact qu’auparavant. Cet été, le groupe était au centre de toutes les attentions, mais la donne a changé depuis que Rockstar a commencé à dévoiler officiellement des images de GTA 6 de manière régulière. Les joueurs ont désormais accès à du contenu officiel, ce qui rend les fuites moins intéressantes. De plus, le risque juridique reste élevé : Rockstar et Take-Two ont déjà engagé des poursuites contre les responsables de fuites, et CyberLeek savait qu’il s’exposait à de lourdes sanctions.
Avec cette annonce, c’est un feuilleton qui prend fin. Les joueurs peuvent désormais attendre sereinement la sortie de GTA 6 , prévue pour le 19 novembre 2026 . Le jeu, développé par Rockstar Games, est l’un des plus attendus de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Les fuites de CyberLeek, bien que spectaculaires, n’auront finalement pas réussi à gâcher l’expérience des fans, qui pourront découvrir le titre dans son intégralité le jour J.
